options.D: The error is that stirring always causes a chemical change, so some salt is always permanently lost

questions.explanation: When salt dissolves in water it forms a solution — the salt particles spread evenly through the water but are not destroyed; they can be recovered by evaporating the water, leaving salt crystals behind, which proves the salt still exists. Option C describes a chemical reaction, but dissolving is a physical change and the salt and water can be separated again, so no new substance is formed.

questions.title: Moon Phases Explained
questions.prompt: Every night for a month, a student draws the shape of the lit part of the Moon she can see. After about 14 days, she sees a full circle. After another 14 days, she is back to seeing almost nothing. What causes these changing shapes?

options.A: Earth's shadow covers different parts of the Moon each night as Earth rotates
options.B: The Moon produces its own light, which it turns on and off in a cycle
options.C: Clouds on the Moon block its surface from view on some nights
options.D: As the Moon orbits Earth, we see different amounts of its sunlit side from our position

questions.explanation: The Moon does not produce its own light — it reflects sunlight, and as it travels around Earth each month, our angle of view changes so we see different portions of the illuminated half, creating the cycle of phases from new moon to full moon and back. Option A confuses moon phases with lunar eclipses, which happen only when Earth's shadow actually falls on the Moon — a rare event, not a nightly one.

questions.title: Heat Transfer by Conduction
questions.prompt: A student leaves a metal key and a plastic ruler on a sunny windowsill for the same amount of time. When she picks them up, the metal key feels much hotter than the plastic ruler, even though both were in the same sunlight. What is the best explanation?

options.A: Metal is darker, so it absorbs more sunlight than the lighter plastic
options.B: Metal is a better conductor of heat and transfers warmth to your hand more quickly than plastic does
options.C: Plastic reflects all sunlight, so it does not heat up at all, while metal absorbs it
options.D: Metal is heavier, and heavier objects always store more heat energy than lighter ones

questions.explanation: Both the metal key and plastic ruler reach similar temperatures in the same sunlight, but metal conducts heat much more efficiently than plastic, so it transfers heat into your hand quickly and feels hotter to the touch — plastic is a poor conductor and transfers heat slowly. Option A (colour) can affect heat absorption, but both objects here are assumed to be in the same conditions and the key concept tested is conduction to the hand, not absorption from sunlight.

questions.title: Living and Non-Living Things
questions.prompt: A student is deciding whether a candle flame should be classified as living or non-living. The flame uses fuel, produces waste gases, grows larger, and can make new flames from other candles. Which statement best evaluates whether the flame is living?

options.A: The flame is living because it grows, uses energy, and can spread to create more flames
options.B: The flame is non-living because it cannot sense its environment, is not made of cells, and cannot reproduce on its own
options.C: The flame is living because it needs oxygen to survive, just like animals do
options.D: The flame is non-living only because it eventually goes out and dies

questions.explanation: Living things must carry out all seven life processes including being made of cells, responding to stimuli, and reproducing independently — a flame satisfies none of these; it is a chemical reaction, not an organism made of cells. Option A is a common misconception because the flame appears to share some life-like qualities, but growth and energy use alone are not enough to classify something as living without the full set of characteristics.

questions.title: Pushes, Pulls and Motion
questions.prompt: A toy car is rolling across a smooth floor and slowing down by itself. No one is touching it. A student says 'nothing is pushing on the car, so forces are not involved.' Evaluate this claim.

options.A: The claim is correct, because objects slow down naturally when no one pushes them
options.B: The claim is incorrect, because gravity is pulling the car sideways and slowing it down
options.C: The claim is incorrect, because friction between the wheels and the floor is a force that acts against the car's motion and slows it
options.D: The claim is correct, because forces only matter when an object is speeding up, not slowing down

questions.explanation: Friction is a force that acts between any two surfaces in contact and always opposes motion, so the floor's friction on the toy car's wheels is what gradually slows it — forces are involved whenever an object changes its speed or direction, whether speeding up or slowing down. Option A reflects the misconception that slowing down is the 'natural' state requiring no force, which was disproved by Newton's first law.

questions.title: Seed Dispersal Methods
questions.prompt: A maple tree produces seeds with wing-like flaps that spin as they fall. A coconut palm produces large seeds that float and are carried by ocean currents. What do both of these strategies have in common, and why is this important for the plants?

options.A: Both strategies use animals to carry seeds away from the parent plant
options.B: Both strategies help seeds travel away from the parent plant to reduce competition for light, water, and space
options.C: Both strategies protect seeds from being eaten by insects during the winter months
options.D: Both strategies allow seeds to germinate faster because they are exposed to more sunlight while travelling

questions.explanation: Both wind dispersal (maple wings) and water dispersal (coconut floating) move seeds away from the parent plant, reducing competition for resources like sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil — plants growing too close together would compete for the same limited resources. Option A is incorrect because neither strategy described uses animals; animal dispersal typically involves seeds attached to fur or eaten inside fruit.

questions.title: Changing and Reversible Processes
questions.prompt: Compare melting chocolate and burning wood. Both involve a change, but one change can be reversed and one cannot. Which option correctly identifies which is reversible and explains why?

options.A: Burning wood is reversible because the ash can be pressed back into a log with enough force
options.B: Melting chocolate is reversible because cooling it causes it to solidify into chocolate again; burning wood is irreversible because new substances like ash and gases are formed
options.C: Both changes are irreversible because heat is involved in both, and heat always causes permanent change
options.D: Melting chocolate is irreversible because the chocolate changes shape; burning wood is reversible because fire can start again

questions.explanation: Melting is a physical change — the chocolate changes state but its chemical composition stays the same, so cooling it returns it to solid chocolate; burning is a chemical change that produces entirely new substances (ash, carbon dioxide, water vapour) that cannot be recombined into wood. Option C confuses the involvement of heat with the type of change — heat can cause both reversible physical changes and irreversible chemical changes.

questions.title: Day and Night Cycle
questions.prompt: A student thinks that night happens because the Moon moves in front of the Sun and blocks its light. What is the actual reason we have day and night, and what is wrong with the student's idea?

options.A: The student is correct; the Moon blocks the Sun every night as it moves across the sky
options.B: Day and night happen because Earth revolves around the Sun once every 24 hours, carrying us in and out of sunlight
options.C: Day and night happen because Earth rotates on its own axis once every 24 hours, so each side faces toward and then away from the Sun
options.D: Day and night happen because the Sun moves around Earth, lighting different parts as it goes

questions.explanation: Earth spins on its own axis once approximately every 24 hours — the side facing the Sun experiences day while the opposite side, facing away, experiences night; the Moon blocking the Sun only happens during a solar eclipse, which is a rare event, not something that occurs every night. Option B confuses rotation (spinning on its axis) with revolution (orbiting the Sun), which takes one year, not one day.

questions.title: Animal Classification Features
questions.prompt: A student is sorting animals into groups. She places a bat with birds because both can fly. Her teacher says the bat belongs in a different group. What feature determines the correct group for the bat, and why does flying not determine its classification?

options.A: Bats belong with birds because both have wings, and wings are the most important classification feature
options.B: Bats are mammals because they have fur, feed their young with milk, and give birth to live young — flying is a behaviour, not a body structure used for classification
options.C: Bats are reptiles because they are cold-blooded and come out mainly at night like many reptiles
options.D: Bats are insects because they are small and have wings like many insects do

questions.explanation: Bats are mammals: they are warm-blooded, covered in fur, give birth to live young, and nurse them with milk — these internal and reproductive characteristics define the mammal group, not the ability to fly; birds are classified separately because they have feathers, lay eggs, and have a different body structure. Flying is a shared ability (convergent feature) that evolved independently in bats, birds, and insects, so it cannot be used to place animals in the same classification group.

questions.title: Magnets and Everyday Uses
questions.prompt: A student tests several objects and finds that only some are attracted to a magnet. She tests copper coins, steel paper clips, aluminium foil, and iron nails. Which objects will be attracted to the magnet, and why are the others not?

options.A: All metals are attracted to magnets, so all four objects will be attracted
options.B: Only shiny objects are attracted to magnets, so the aluminium foil and copper coins will be attracted
options.C: Steel paper clips and iron nails will be attracted, because magnets attract iron and steel; copper and aluminium are metals but are not magnetic
options.D: Only the iron nails will be attracted, because steel is not a natural metal and does not respond to magnets

questions.explanation: Magnets attract ferromagnetic materials — primarily iron, steel (which contains iron), nickel, and cobalt; copper and aluminium are metals but are not ferromagnetic, so they are not attracted to ordinary magnets. Option A is the classic misconception that all metals are magnetic, which is incorrect — many everyday metals like copper, gold, silver, and aluminium are not attracted to magnets at all.

questions.title: Environmental Impact of Humans
questions.prompt: A new road is built through a forest, cutting it into two separate pieces. Scientists notice that the number of certain animal species living there begins to drop, even though the animals are not hunted and food is still available. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: Animals are frightened by the colour of the road surface and choose to move to new forests
options.B: The road splits the habitat into smaller sections, limiting how far animals can move to find mates, food, and shelter, reducing their chances of survival
options.C: The new road brings more sunlight into the forest, making it too hot for animals to survive
options.D: Animals stop eating when a road is nearby because the smell of tar removes their appetite

questions.explanation: Habitat fragmentation caused by roads reduces the total area of connected habitat and creates barriers that prevent animals from moving freely to find mates, territory, and food sources, which reduces populations over time even when hunting is not occurring. Option C has a small element of truth (roads can affect microclimate slightly) but is not the primary reason — habitat connectivity and movement barriers are the main ecological concern in fragmentation studies.

questions.title: Fair Testing in Science
questions.prompt: Two students want to find out whether a ball rolls further on a wooden floor or a carpeted floor. Student A rolls the ball from the same height on a ramp each time. Student B rolls one ball by hand and the other using a ramp. Which student's test is fair, and what makes it fair or unfair?

options.A: Student B's test is fairer because using different methods shows more variety in the results
options.B: Student A's test is fair because only the floor surface is different — all other conditions are kept the same
options.C: Both tests are equally fair because they are both testing the same two floor surfaces
options.D: Student B's test is fairer because rolling by hand is more natural and gives more realistic results

questions.explanation: In a fair test, only one variable (the floor surface) is changed while all others (such as how the ball is released, the ball used, and the starting height) are kept the same — Student A achieves this by using the same ramp at the same height every time. Student B's test is unfair because two variables are changed at once (floor surface and method of rolling), meaning we cannot know whether different results are caused by the surface or the launching method.

questions.title: Humans and Body Systems
questions.prompt: When you run fast, your heart beats faster and you breathe more quickly. A student says these two changes are unrelated. Evaluate this claim and explain the connection between the two changes.

options.A: The claim is correct — breathing faster cools you down while the heart beats faster to warm the muscles, and these are separate jobs
options.B: The claim is incorrect — muscles use more oxygen when working hard, so the lungs breathe faster to bring in more oxygen and the heart beats faster to pump that oxygen-rich blood to the muscles
options.C: The claim is incorrect — the lungs breathe faster to remove extra blood from the body, and the heart beats faster to push that blood out
options.D: The claim is correct — the heart and lungs work independently and only happen to speed up at the same time by coincidence

questions.explanation: The circulatory and respiratory systems work together: during exercise, muscles need more oxygen to release energy, so the lungs increase their breathing rate to take in more oxygen, and the heart beats faster to circulate the oxygen-rich blood to those working muscles more quickly. Option A incorrectly separates the two systems and assigns them wrong functions — breathing is primarily for gas exchange, not cooling.

questions.title: Heat Transfer Methods
questions.prompt: A warm radiator heats a cold room. Air near the radiator rises and cool air moves in to take its place. What is the name of this method of heat transfer, and why does the warm air rise?

options.A: Conduction — the warm air conducts heat directly to the cool air above it
options.B: Convection — warm air becomes less dense and rises, while denser cool air sinks
options.C: Radiation — the radiator sends heat rays that push warm air upward
options.D: Convection — warm air becomes heavier and rises because it has more energy

questions.explanation: Convection occurs in fluids like air because heating makes particles spread apart, reducing density, so warm air floats upward and cooler, denser air sinks to replace it. Option D is wrong because warm air is actually less dense and lighter, not heavier — it is the reduced density, not increased weight, that causes rising.

questions.title: Plant Photosynthesis Inputs
questions.prompt: A student claims: 'Plants make their food entirely from the water and minerals they absorb through their roots.' Evaluate this claim. What important ingredient is the student leaving out?

options.A: The student is wrong — plants also need oxygen from the air to make food
options.B: The student is wrong — plants also need carbon dioxide from the air to make food
options.C: The student is correct — water and minerals are all that plants need to grow
options.D: The student is wrong — plants also need nitrogen from the air to make food

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis requires carbon dioxide from the air, water, and light energy — plants combine CO₂ and water to produce glucose. Oxygen is released as a byproduct, not used as an ingredient, making option A incorrect even though oxygen is connected to photosynthesis.

questions.title: States of Matter Changes
questions.prompt: Ice is left in a warm room and slowly turns to liquid water. Then the water is heated strongly and turns to water vapour. Which correctly describes what happens to the water particles during both changes?

options.A: The particles get bigger as they absorb heat energy in both changes
options.B: The particles move faster and spread farther apart in both changes
options.C: New types of particles are created when ice becomes water and when water becomes vapour
options.D: The particles move faster when ice melts but slow down when water becomes vapour

questions.explanation: During melting and evaporation, heat energy increases particle movement; the particles remain the same water molecules but move faster and move farther apart each time. Particles do not change size or type — the same H₂O molecules are present in all three states, ruling out options A and C.

questions.title: Food Chain Energy Flow
questions.prompt: In a food chain, grass is eaten by a grasshopper, which is eaten by a frog, which is eaten by a hawk. At which step is the LEAST amount of energy available, and why?

options.A: At the grasshopper, because insects are small and cannot store much energy
options.B: At the hawk, because energy is lost at every step along the chain
options.C: At the grass, because plants produce less energy than animals do
options.D: At the frog, because frogs release the most heat of any animal in the chain

questions.explanation: Energy is lost as heat and in life processes at every link in a food chain, so the organism at the end — the hawk — has access to the least energy. Grass actually holds the most energy as the producer; the small size of grasshoppers does not determine energy availability in the chain.

questions.title: Dissolving and Mixtures
questions.prompt: Salt is stirred into warm water until no grains are visible. A student says the salt has disappeared. Which statement best explains why the student is wrong, and how the salt could be recovered?

options.A: The salt changed into water, but it can be turned back into salt by cooling the mixture
options.B: The salt broke into tiny particles spread through the water, and evaporating the water would leave the salt behind
options.C: The salt dissolved by turning into a gas, and the gas can be trapped and cooled to recover the salt
options.D: The salt mixed with water particles to make a new substance, which cannot be separated again

questions.explanation: Dissolving is a physical change — salt particles spread evenly through the water but remain salt; evaporating the water leaves the solid salt crystals behind. Dissolving does not create a new substance and cannot be reversed simply by cooling, which is what would reverse freezing, not dissolving.

questions.title: Moon Phases Explained
questions.prompt: The Moon does not produce its own light. Yet we see it shining brightly at night. What causes the Moon to appear bright, and why do we see different amounts of the lit side at different times of the month?

options.A: The Moon reflects sunlight, and we see different phases because Earth's shadow covers different parts of the Moon each night
options.B: The Moon reflects sunlight, and we see different phases because the Moon orbits Earth, changing which part of its lit side faces us
options.C: The Moon glows from stored heat, and phases occur because clouds on Earth block different parts of the Moon
options.D: The Moon reflects Earthlight, and we see different phases because the Moon spins on its axis once every week

questions.explanation: The Moon reflects sunlight, and as it orbits Earth over about 29 days, we see varying portions of its sunlit half — this creates the cycle of phases. Earth's shadow on the Moon is a lunar eclipse, which is a separate rare event, not the cause of regular monthly phases.

questions.title: Gravity and Falling Objects
questions.prompt: A student drops a large rock and a small pebble from the same height at the same moment. Ignoring air resistance, which hits the ground first, and why?

options.A: The large rock, because gravity pulls harder on heavier objects so they fall faster
options.B: The small pebble, because lighter objects meet less air resistance and fall faster
options.C: They hit at the same time, because gravity accelerates all objects equally regardless of mass
options.D: The large rock, because it has more momentum pushing it downward

questions.explanation: Without air resistance, gravity accelerates every object at the same rate — about 10 m/s² on Earth — regardless of mass, so both objects land simultaneously. The common belief that heavier objects fall faster confuses gravitational force with gravitational acceleration; a heavier object feels more gravitational pull but also has more mass to move, so the effect cancels out.

questions.title: Adaptation and Survival
questions.prompt: A polar bear has thick white fur, a thick layer of fat under its skin, and small rounded ears. Which combination of these features is MOST important for reducing heat loss in an Arctic environment, and why?

options.A: White fur and small ears — the white colour reflects heat inward and small ears reduce camouflage surface
options.B: Thick fat and small ears — fat insulates the body and small ears mean less surface area to lose heat
options.C: White fur and thick fat — white fur absorbs sunlight well and fat provides energy in winter
options.D: Small ears and white fur — small ears prevent frostbite and white fur is lighter so easier to move in

questions.explanation: Fat beneath the skin acts as excellent insulation trapping body heat, and small ears reduce the surface area through which heat is radiated away — both directly limit heat loss. White fur helps with camouflage for hunting but does not reflect heat inward; fur's hollow shafts do help insulation, but fat and ear size are the primary heat-retention adaptations.

questions.title: Rock Cycle Processes
questions.prompt: A geologist finds a rock that has visible layers of different materials and contains fossils of ancient shells. What type of rock is this, and how did it most likely form?

options.A: Igneous rock, formed when layers of lava cooled slowly underground over millions of years
options.B: Metamorphic rock, formed when existing rock was squeezed and heated until it changed form
options.C: Sedimentary rock, formed when layers of tiny particles settled and were pressed together over time
options.D: Metamorphic rock, formed when shells were buried and melted by underground heat

questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form when sediment — tiny pieces of rock, minerals, and organic material — is deposited in layers and compacted over long periods; fossils are preserved in this process as organisms get buried in sediment. Igneous rocks form from cooled magma and rarely contain fossils, and metamorphic rocks form under intense heat and pressure that would destroy fossil evidence.

questions.title: Sound Transmission Media
questions.prompt: Two students hold opposite ends of a long metal rail. One student taps the rail with a hammer. The other student hears two sounds — one arriving sooner than the other. What best explains why two sounds are heard?

options.A: Sound travels through the metal rail faster than through the air, so two separate sounds arrive at different times
options.B: The hammer makes two sounds — one going into the metal and one bouncing off it into the air
options.C: Sound travels slower through metal than air, so the metal sound arrives after the air sound
options.D: The echo from the ground arrives at the same time as the sound through the metal, making two sounds

questions.explanation: Sound travels much faster through solids than through gases — approximately 5000 m/s in steel compared to about 340 m/s in air — so the vibration through the rail reaches the listener's ear well before the sound wave through the air does. Option C has the relationship reversed; solids transmit sound faster than air, not slower.

questions.title: Water Cycle Processes
questions.prompt: On a cold morning, a student notices water droplets forming on the outside of a glass of ice water. The student says the glass must be leaking. What is the correct explanation for the droplets?

options.A: Water from inside the glass seeps through tiny holes in the glass onto the outside surface
options.B: Water vapour in the air near the cold glass loses energy, slows down, and condenses into liquid droplets
options.C: The cold glass freezes the air around it, which melts and drips down the outside
options.D: Water vapour from inside the glass escapes and condenses on the cooler outer surface

questions.explanation: Condensation occurs when warm, moist air contacts a cold surface — the air loses thermal energy, water vapour particles slow down enough to become liquid water on the outside of the glass. The water comes from the surrounding air, not from inside the glass; air does not freeze and melt in this scenario, it is the water vapour that changes state.

questions.title: Electrical Conductors
questions.prompt: A student tests several materials by placing each one between two wires connected to a battery and a bulb. The bulb lights up for copper wire and salty water, but not for distilled water or rubber. What conclusion can the student correctly draw?

options.A: Only metals can conduct electricity, because salty water conducted due to the dissolved metal particles in the salt
options.B: Liquids conduct electricity only when they are heated, because salty water must have been warm
options.C: Materials that allow electric current to flow through them are conductors; dissolved salts in water allow it to conduct
options.D: Conductors must be shiny, which is why copper and salty water both conducted electricity

questions.explanation: Electrical conductors allow current to flow through them; when salt dissolves in water it releases charged particles called ions that carry the electric current, which is why salty water conducts but pure distilled water does not. Salt is not a metal — it is sodium chloride — so option A's reasoning is incorrect even though copper's conductivity is correct.

questions.title: Habitat and Ecosystem Change
questions.prompt: A new motorway is built through the middle of a large forest, splitting it into two smaller patches. Scientists predict this will reduce the number of large animal species over time, even though trees remain on both sides. Why?

options.A: The noise and light from the motorway will change the weather on both sides of the road
options.B: Smaller, isolated habitat patches support smaller populations that cannot find mates or resources across the barrier
options.C: The road will cause acid rain that poisons the trees on both sides of the motorway
options.D: Large animals will move to the smaller patches and eat all the food, causing species to die out

questions.explanation: Habitat fragmentation reduces the effective range of large animals that need wide territories; isolated populations may be too small to survive, and individuals cannot travel across the dangerous road to find mates or seasonal resources. Noise and light do affect some animals but are not the primary scientific reason biodiversity falls in fragmented habitats.

questions.title: Light Refraction Basics
questions.prompt: A pencil is placed in a glass of water and viewed from the side. The pencil appears to bend at the water's surface. A student says the pencil is actually bending. What is the correct scientific explanation?

options.A: The pencil is not bending; light changes direction as it moves from water into air, making the pencil appear bent
options.B: The pencil is not bending; the water magnifies the lower part of the pencil, shifting its apparent position
options.C: The pencil is not bending; the reflection of the pencil in the glass creates a second image that looks displaced
options.D: The pencil is not bending; water absorbs part of the light from the pencil, making it look shorter and angled

questions.explanation: Refraction is the bending of light rays as they pass from one medium to another with different density — light travels more slowly in water than in air and changes direction at the surface, making the submerged part appear shifted. While water can magnify slightly, the apparent bend is specifically caused by the change in light's direction at the air-water boundary, not magnification alone.

questions.title: Pollination and Reproduction
questions.prompt: Some flowers are brightly coloured and produce sweet nectar. Others are dull-coloured, have no nectar, and release huge amounts of pollen into the air. What does this difference tell us about how each type of flower is most likely pollinated?

options.A: Bright flowers are pollinated by animals; dull flowers that release large amounts of pollen rely on wind
options.B: Bright flowers are pollinated by wind because colours help pollen travel; dull flowers rely on insects
options.C: Both types are pollinated by insects — bright ones attract bees and dull ones attract moths at night
options.D: Dull flowers are pollinated by animals that prefer less colour; bright flowers self-pollinate using nectar

questions.explanation: Animal-pollinated flowers have evolved bright colours and nectar to attract insects or birds that carry pollen between flowers; wind-pollinated flowers do not need to attract animals so they are dull and produce vast quantities of lightweight pollen to increase the chance of wind carrying some to another flower. Bright colours are signals to animals, not an aid for wind travel, so option B has the logic reversed.

questions.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
questions.prompt: A book sits still on a table. A student says no forces are acting on the book because it is not moving. Identify the error in the student's reasoning.

options.A: The student is wrong — gravity pulls the book down and the table pushes up equally, so two forces act on it and they balance
options.B: The student is wrong — only gravity acts on the book, and gravity alone is enough to keep it still
options.C: The student is correct — objects that are not moving have no forces acting on them at all
options.D: The student is wrong — friction from the table is the only force acting on the book, keeping it in place

questions.explanation: A stationary object on a surface has at least two forces acting on it: gravity pulling it downward and the normal reaction force from the surface pushing upward — these forces are equal and opposite, so they balance and result in no movement. The absence of motion means forces are balanced, not that forces are absent; gravity acts on all objects with mass near Earth.

questions.title: Animal Life Cycles
questions.prompt: A butterfly starts as an egg, becomes a caterpillar, forms a chrysalis, and then emerges as a butterfly. A grasshopper starts as an egg, hatches into a small version of itself, and gradually grows into an adult. What is the key difference between these two types of life cycle?

options.A: The butterfly undergoes complete metamorphosis with a pupal stage; the grasshopper undergoes incomplete metamorphosis with no pupal stage
options.B: The butterfly reproduces faster because its chrysalis stage shortens the time between generations
options.C: The grasshopper undergoes complete metamorphosis because it changes size; the butterfly does not change size after emerging
options.D: Both life cycles are the same type, but the butterfly has an extra feeding stage to build up more energy

questions.explanation: Complete metamorphosis has four distinct stages — egg, larva, pupa, adult — and the larva looks completely different from the adult; incomplete metamorphosis has three stages where young, called nymphs, resemble small adults and gradually change without a pupal stage. The chrysalis is the pupal stage, which grasshoppers skip entirely — they do not experience a dramatic body restructuring.

questions.title: Magnets and Magnetic Fields
questions.prompt: A student discovers that a magnet can attract a steel paper clip without touching it. She then places a sheet of cardboard between the magnet and the clip and the clip still moves. What does this experiment demonstrate about magnetic force?

options.A: Magnetic force only works through non-metal materials like cardboard; metals block the force completely
options.B: Magnetic force can act at a distance and can pass through non-magnetic materials such as cardboard
options.C: The cardboard becomes magnetised and passes on the magnetic force to the paper clip
options.D: The magnet's force travels through the air around the cardboard to reach the clip

questions.explanation: Magnetic fields extend through space and can pass through non-magnetic materials including cardboard, wood, and plastic without significant weakening — this is why magnetic force can act at a distance through barriers. The cardboard does not become magnetised; it is simply transparent to the magnetic field, and the force is not redirected around the cardboard.

questions.title: Fair Test Design
questions.prompt: Two students investigate whether dark-coloured containers cool down faster than light-coloured containers. Student A uses a large black tin and a small white cup. Student B uses two identical tins, one painted black and one painted white. Which student's investigation is more scientific, and why?

options.A: Student A, because using different sizes means more variables are tested at the same time
options.B: Student B, because changing only the colour keeps all other variables the same, making it a fair test
options.C: Student A, because a larger black container will show a bigger temperature change that is easier to measure
options.D: Both are equally valid because both investigations compare a dark and a light container

questions.explanation: A fair test requires only one variable to be changed — here, colour — while all others such as size, material, and starting temperature remain the same; Student B controls these variables by using identical tins. Student A changes both colour and size simultaneously, so any difference in cooling could be due to size rather than colour, making the results unreliable.

questions.title: Soil and Erosion
questions.prompt: A scientist compares two hillsides: one covered in grass and plants, the other bare soil with no vegetation. After heavy rainfall, much more soil washes away from the bare hillside. Why do plant roots help prevent soil erosion?

options.A: Plant roots absorb all the rainwater before it can reach the soil, so no water touches the soil particles
options.B: Plant roots bind soil particles together, and leaves slow the impact of raindrops on the soil surface
options.C: Plants change the chemical composition of the soil, making soil particles stick together with a natural glue
options.D: Plant roots push soil deeper underground, where it cannot be washed away by surface water

questions.explanation: Plant roots physically hold soil particles together in a network, preventing water from loosening and carrying them away; leaves and stems also reduce the kinetic energy of raindrops before they hit the soil. Roots do not absorb all rainfall — much still infiltrates the soil — and the mechanism is physical binding, not chemical change.

questions.title: Reflection and Mirrors
questions.prompt: A student shines a torch at a flat mirror at an angle. She notices the reflected beam leaves the mirror at the same angle on the other side. If she tilts the mirror so the beam hits it more steeply, what will happen to the reflected beam?

options.A: The reflected beam will travel in the same direction as before because mirrors always reflect light the same way
options.B: The reflected beam will also leave at a steeper angle, following the law that the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence
options.C: The reflected beam will scatter in all directions because hitting the mirror more steeply disrupts the reflection
options.D: The reflected beam will slow down and become dimmer because a steeper angle reduces the energy of reflected light

questions.explanation: The law of reflection states that the angle at which light hits a mirror equals the angle at which it bounces off — both angles are measured from the perpendicular to the mirror surface; if the angle of incidence increases, the angle of reflection increases equally. The direction of the reflected beam always changes when the mirror is tilted, so option A is incorrect.

questions.title: Human Body Digestion
questions.prompt: Food takes a long journey through the human body. Which correctly describes the main role of the small intestine in digestion, and how it is suited to that role?

options.A: The small intestine breaks food into large chunks using strong muscles; its long length gives food enough time to be torn apart
options.B: The small intestine absorbs nutrients into the blood; its long length and folded inner walls give a very large surface area for absorption
options.C: The small intestine stores food until the body needs energy; its coiled shape lets it hold large amounts of food
options.D: The small intestine produces stomach acid to dissolve food; its narrow shape concentrates the acid for maximum effect

questions.explanation: The small intestine is the main site of nutrient absorption — digested food molecules pass through its walls into the bloodstream; its great length (about 6–7 metres) and tiny finger-like projections called villi create a huge surface area that maximises absorption. Stomach acid is produced in the stomach, not the small intestine, making option D incorrect.

questions.title: Weather Patterns and Air
questions.prompt: A meteorologist says: 'Low pressure systems are usually associated with cloudy, wet weather, while high pressure systems bring clear, dry conditions.' What best explains why low pressure leads to clouds and rain?

options.A: In a low pressure system, cold air sinks and compresses, causing water vapour to heat up and form storm clouds
options.B: In a low pressure system, warm air rises, cools as it goes higher, and water vapour condenses to form clouds and rain
options.C: In a low pressure system, the reduced weight of air allows more sunlight through, heating the ground and causing rain
options.D: In a low pressure system, air rushes outward from the centre, pulling moisture from the sea and releasing it as rain

questions.explanation: In a low pressure system, air converges near the surface and is forced upward; as it rises it cools, and when it reaches the dew point, water vapour condenses into cloud droplets that can eventually fall as precipitation. High pressure systems cause air to sink and warm, which prevents condensation and produces clear skies — the opposite of option A's description.

questions.title: Seeds and Dispersal
questions.prompt: A sycamore seed has a thin wing attached to it. A coconut has a thick, fibrous, waterproof outer layer. What do both of these features have in common in terms of survival, even though the features look very different?

options.A: Both features help the seed store extra food so the seedling can grow in difficult conditions
options.B: Both features help the seed travel away from the parent plant so it can grow with less competition
options.C: Both features protect the seed from being eaten by animals while it remains near the parent plant
options.D: Both features help the seed absorb water quickly once it lands in a suitable place

questions.explanation: Seed dispersal reduces competition for light, water, and nutrients between parent and offspring — the sycamore's wing allows wind dispersal while the coconut's buoyant, waterproof husk allows water dispersal across the ocean; both achieve the same goal of spreading offspring away from the parent. Seed features are primarily about dispersal mechanisms, not protection from predators while stationary.

questions.title: Properties of Materials
questions.prompt: An engineer needs to choose a material for a frying pan handle. She tests wood, rubber, steel, and copper. Which material should she choose, and what property makes it most suitable?

options.A: Copper, because it is a strong metal that will not break when the pan is lifted
options.B: Steel, because it is rigid and will not melt at the temperatures used in cooking
options.C: Wood, because it is a poor conductor of heat so the handle stays cool and safe to grip
options.D: Rubber, because it is flexible and will absorb heat before it reaches the person's hand

questions.explanation: Wood is a thermal insulator — it conducts heat very poorly — so a wooden handle stays at a safe temperature even when the pan is over a flame; this is the key property needed for a handle that must be touched safely. Copper and steel are excellent heat conductors, meaning they would transfer dangerous heat to a person's hand, even if they are strong materials.

questions.title: Heat Transfer Methods
questions.prompt: A metal pot of water is placed on a hot stove. The bottom of the pot gets hot first, then the water near the bottom heats up and rises while cooler water sinks. What is the name of this process that moves heat through the water?

options.A: Conduction, because the metal touches the water directly
options.B: Convection, because warm water rises and cool water sinks in a cycle
options.C: Radiation, because heat energy travels through the water as waves
options.D: Insulation, because the pot traps the heat inside the water

questions.explanation: Convection is the transfer of heat through a fluid (liquid or gas) by the movement of the fluid itself — warm water becomes less dense and rises, while cooler, denser water sinks, creating a convection current. Conduction is a plausible distractor because it does occur where the metal pot touches the water, but it does not describe the circular movement through the water that the question is asking about.

questions.title: Plant Life Cycles
questions.prompt: A student says: 'Seeds can only grow into new plants if an animal carries them to a new place.' Evaluate this claim. Is the student correct?

options.A: Correct, because all seeds need to travel away from the parent plant to get enough sunlight
options.B: Correct, because seeds cannot sprout unless they pass through an animal's digestive system first
options.C: Incorrect, because seeds can also be dispersed by wind, water, or by bursting open on their own
options.D: Incorrect, because most seeds grow best directly under the parent plant where the soil is already fertile

questions.explanation: Seed dispersal happens through many methods including wind (dandelion seeds), water (coconuts), and explosive pods (peas), not only through animals. Option A is a plausible distractor because competition for sunlight is a real reason dispersal helps plants, but it wrongly states animals are the only dispersal method.

questions.title: States of Matter Changes
questions.prompt: Water turns into ice in a freezer. A student claims that freezing destroys water molecules and creates brand-new ice molecules. What is wrong with this claim?

options.A: Nothing is wrong — freezing does change water molecules into a different type of molecule called ice
options.B: The claim is wrong because freezing only removes colour from water molecules, not their structure
options.C: The claim is wrong because freezing just slows the water molecules down and rearranges them — the molecules stay the same
options.D: The claim is wrong because ice is not actually made of water molecules but of oxygen atoms only

questions.explanation: Freezing is a physical change, not a chemical one — the water molecules (H₂O) remain identical, but they slow down and lock into a rigid crystalline arrangement. Option A is the top distractor because students often confuse physical state changes with chemical changes that produce new substances.

questions.title: Food Chains and Energy
questions.prompt: In a meadow food chain: grass → grasshopper → frog → hawk. A disease kills most of the frogs. What would most likely happen to the grasshopper population first?

options.A: The grasshopper population would decrease because hawks would start eating grasshoppers instead
options.B: The grasshopper population would increase because fewer frogs would be eating them
options.C: The grasshopper population would stay the same because frogs are not their main predator
options.D: The grasshopper population would decrease because the disease would spread from frogs to grasshoppers

questions.explanation: With fewer predators (frogs) eating grasshoppers, the grasshopper population loses population control and numbers rise — this is a classic predator-prey relationship. Option A is a strong distractor because hawks might adapt their diet, but the immediate first effect on grasshoppers is the loss of their direct predator, causing an increase rather than decrease.

questions.title: Light and Transparent Materials
questions.prompt: A student shines a torch at three materials: clear glass, frosted glass, and a wooden board. She can see a clear image through the clear glass, a blurry glow through the frosted glass, and nothing through the wood. What correctly describes frosted glass?

options.A: Transparent, because some light passes through it
options.B: Opaque, because you cannot see a clear image through it
options.C: Translucent, because it lets light through but scatters it so no clear image forms
options.D: Reflective, because the frosted surface bounces light back to the observer

questions.explanation: Translucent materials allow light to pass through but scatter it, producing a glow without a clear image — frosted glass is the classic example of this property. Option A is a strong distractor because frosted glass does transmit light, but 'transparent' specifically requires that a clear image can be seen, which frosted glass does not allow.

questions.title: Gravity and Falling Objects
questions.prompt: A student drops a large rock and a small pebble from the same height at exactly the same moment. Ignoring air resistance, which one hits the ground first?

options.A: The large rock, because gravity pulls harder on heavier objects
options.B: The small pebble, because it is lighter and meets less air resistance
options.C: They hit at the same time, because gravity accelerates all objects equally regardless of mass
options.D: They hit at the same time, but only because the rock and pebble are made of the same material

questions.explanation: Galileo showed that gravity accelerates all objects at the same rate (9.8 m/s² on Earth) regardless of their mass, so both objects land simultaneously when air resistance is removed. Option A is the most common wrong answer because students intuitively feel heavier objects fall faster, but the greater gravitational force on a heavier object is exactly cancelled by its greater mass.

questions.title: Ecosystem Roles
questions.prompt: A student is sorting organisms into groups: producers, consumers, and decomposers. She is unsure where to place a mushroom growing on a rotting log. Which group does the mushroom belong to, and why?

options.A: Producer, because mushrooms grow from the ground like plants do
options.B: Consumer, because mushrooms absorb nutrients from other organisms
options.C: Decomposer, because mushrooms break down dead organic material to get their energy
options.D: Producer, because mushrooms release oxygen into the air around them

questions.explanation: Fungi like mushrooms are decomposers — they secrete enzymes that break down dead organic matter (such as a rotting log) and absorb the released nutrients, recycling materials back into the ecosystem. Option B is a strong distractor because mushrooms do absorb nutrients from other organisms, but 'consumer' specifically refers to organisms that eat living organisms; decomposers feed on dead material.

questions.title: Electricity and Conductors
questions.prompt: A student tests whether different materials conduct electricity by placing them in a simple circuit with a bulb. The bulb lights up with copper wire and with wet salty water, but not with dry wood. What conclusion is most accurate?

options.A: Only metals can conduct electricity, because dry wood and water are both non-metals
options.B: All liquids conduct electricity, because they allow particles to move freely
options.C: Conductivity depends on the material — some non-metals like salty water can conduct electricity
options.D: Wood would also conduct electricity if the circuit used a stronger battery

questions.explanation: Electrical conductivity depends on whether a material has free-moving charged particles — metals have free electrons, and salty water has dissolved ions, both of which allow current to flow. Option A is wrong because salty water (a non-metal liquid) also conducts, disproving the claim that only metals can conduct electricity.

questions.title: Water Cycle Processes
questions.prompt: On a cold morning, a student notices water droplets forming on the outside of a chilled glass of juice. Her friend says the glass must be leaking. What is actually happening, and what is this process called?

options.A: Evaporation — water from inside the glass is escaping slowly through tiny holes in the glass
options.B: Condensation — water vapour from the air cools when it touches the cold glass and turns into liquid
options.C: Precipitation — water droplets in the air are heavy enough to fall and land on the glass
options.D: Transpiration — the glass is releasing water that was absorbed from the juice inside

questions.explanation: Condensation occurs when warm, moisture-laden air contacts a cold surface, causing water vapour to lose energy and change into liquid water droplets on the outside of the glass. Option A is the top distractor because students may think water is escaping from inside, but the droplets form from water vapour already in the surrounding air, not from the juice.

questions.title: Animal Adaptations
questions.prompt: A polar bear has white fur, a thick layer of fat under its skin, and small rounded ears. A student says the white fur is the most important cold-weather adaptation. Evaluate this claim.

options.A: Correct — white fur reflects sunlight and keeps the bear much warmer than dark fur would
options.B: Correct — white fur traps more air than dark fur and provides the most insulation
options.C: Incorrect — the thick layer of fat is likely more important because it provides the main insulation against freezing temperatures
options.D: Incorrect — the small ears are the most important adaptation because they lose the least heat of all the features

questions.explanation: The blubber layer in polar bears can be up to 11 cm thick and is the primary insulator against Arctic cold, retaining core body heat even in freezing water. The white fur is mainly for camouflage and provides some insulation, but it is not the most critical warmth adaptation, making C correct. Option D is a plausible distractor because small ears do reduce heat loss (less surface area), but the fat layer is a far more powerful insulator.

questions.title: Forces and Motion
questions.prompt: A student pushes a toy car along a table and then lets go. The car slows down and stops. She says: 'The car stopped because the pushing force ran out.' What is the real reason the car stopped?

options.A: Gravity pulled the car downward into the table, which cancelled its forward motion
options.B: Friction between the car's wheels and the table surface acted against the car's motion and slowed it down
options.C: The car used up its stored energy while moving and had none left to keep going
options.D: Air pressure pushed against the front of the car and gradually brought it to a stop

questions.explanation: Once the push is removed, friction — the force between the wheels and the table surface — acts in the opposite direction to the car's motion, removing kinetic energy and slowing the car to a stop. Option C is a strong distractor because students often think of motion as requiring a fuel-like energy store that 'runs out,' but objects would continue moving forever without friction (Newton's first law).

questions.title: Human Body Systems
questions.prompt: A student claims that the heart pumps blood only to the lungs and back, and that is its only job. Identify the error in this claim.

options.A: There is no error — the heart only moves blood between itself and the lungs
options.B: The error is that the heart does not pump blood to the lungs at all — lungs move air, not blood
options.C: The error is that the heart pumps blood to the entire body, not just the lungs — it delivers oxygen and nutrients to all organs and tissues
options.D: The error is that the heart's main job is to filter waste from the blood, not to pump it

questions.explanation: The heart has two pumping circuits: pulmonary circulation (to the lungs to collect oxygen) and systemic circulation (to all other body organs and tissues to deliver oxygen and nutrients). The student's claim only describes the pulmonary circuit and ignores systemic circulation entirely. Option B is wrong because the heart does pump blood to the lungs — that part of the student's statement is actually correct.

questions.title: Rocks and Erosion
questions.prompt: A river carries small pieces of rock and deposits them at its mouth where it meets the sea. Over millions of years, layers of these pieces are compressed and cemented together. What type of rock forms this way?

options.A: Igneous rock, because it forms from materials that were once broken down and re-formed
options.B: Metamorphic rock, because heat and pressure deep underground change the rock's structure
options.C: Sedimentary rock, because it forms from layers of sediment — small pieces of material deposited and compacted over time
options.D: Volcanic rock, because rivers often flow near volcanoes and pick up lava fragments

questions.explanation: Sedimentary rock forms when layers of sediment (sand, gravel, shells, or other fragments) are deposited, compressed, and cemented together over long periods — sandstone and limestone are common examples. Option B is a strong distractor because metamorphic rock also involves pressure, but metamorphic rock forms when existing rock is transformed by heat and pressure deep inside the Earth, not by surface deposition.

questions.title: Sound Vibration
questions.prompt: Two students are on opposite ends of a long metal fence. Student A taps the fence with a stone. Student B presses her ear to the fence and also listens through the air. Through which medium does the sound reach her first, and why?

options.A: Through the air, because air carries sound waves in all directions at once
options.B: Through the metal fence, because sound travels faster through solids than through gases
options.C: They arrive at exactly the same time, because sound speed depends only on the distance travelled
options.D: Through the metal fence, because metal vibrates more loudly than air and loudness increases speed

questions.explanation: Sound travels much faster through solids than gases because the particles in a solid are more tightly packed, allowing vibrations to pass between them more quickly — sound travels at about 5,100 m/s in steel compared to about 340 m/s in air. Option D is a plausible distractor because students may connect loudness to speed, but loudness (amplitude) and speed are separate properties; it is the density and elasticity of the medium that determines speed.

questions.title: Photosynthesis Ingredients
questions.prompt: A student grows two identical plants. She gives Plant A water, light, and air. She gives Plant B water and air, but covers it with a completely dark box. After two weeks, Plant B is wilting and turning yellow. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: Plant B could not absorb water through its roots because darkness prevents root function
options.B: Plant B could not make its own food through photosynthesis because it had no light energy to drive the process
options.C: Plant B ran out of carbon dioxide because the dark box stopped fresh air from reaching it
options.D: Plant B's leaves dried out because darkness causes faster water loss through tiny pores called stomata

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis requires light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose — without light, Plant B cannot produce food and its stored energy runs out, causing wilting and yellowing (chlorophyll breaks down). Option C is a strong distractor because CO₂ availability is also needed for photosynthesis, but the student is told Plant B still receives air, so the missing factor is light, not carbon dioxide.

questions.title: Changing Materials
questions.prompt: A student burns a piece of paper. Another student folds a piece of paper. Which change can be reversed, and what type of change is burning?

options.A: Burning can be reversed; it is a physical change because the paper still exists as ash
options.B: Folding can be reversed; burning is a chemical change because new substances like ash and gases are produced
options.C: Neither can be reversed; both are chemical changes because the shape and appearance of the paper change
options.D: Both can be reversed; folding and burning are both physical changes because no atoms are lost

questions.explanation: Folding is a physical change — the paper's molecules are unchanged and it can be unfolded — while burning is an irreversible chemical change that produces entirely new substances including carbon dioxide gas, water vapour, and ash. Option A is a strong distractor because ash does remain, but the original paper molecules have been permanently altered into new chemical compounds, so it cannot be reversed.

questions.title: Habitats and Survival
questions.prompt: A student compares a cactus in a desert to a water lily in a pond. Both are plants, but they look very different. What is the best explanation for why they have such different features?

options.A: They are different because deserts have more sunlight, and more sunlight causes plants to grow spines instead of wide leaves
options.B: They are different because their features are adaptations that help each plant survive in its specific habitat — the cactus saves water, while the lily absorbs water easily
options.C: They are different because they belong to completely different kingdoms — the cactus is a plant but the water lily is an alga
options.D: They are different because plants in cold habitats develop wide leaves and plants in hot habitats always develop spines

questions.explanation: Adaptations are features that develop over generations to help organisms survive in specific environments — the cactus has thick stems to store water and small or no leaves to reduce water loss, while the water lily has broad flat leaves to maximise light absorption on the water surface. Option A is wrong because sunlight intensity alone does not directly cause spine development; it is the need to conserve scarce water in a dry habitat that drives the cactus's features.

questions.title: Magnets and Everyday Use
questions.prompt: A student tests a variety of objects with a magnet: an iron nail, a copper coin, a steel paper clip, and an aluminium foil ball. Which objects will the magnet attract?

options.A: All four objects, because all metals are attracted to magnets
options.B: The iron nail and steel paper clip only, because magnets attract iron and steel but not all metals
options.C: The iron nail only, because steel is a different material from iron and is not magnetic
options.D: The copper coin and aluminium foil ball only, because lighter metals are easier for magnets to attract

questions.explanation: Magnets attract ferromagnetic materials — primarily iron, steel (which contains iron), nickel, and cobalt — but not all metals. Copper and aluminium are non-magnetic metals. Steel is an iron-based alloy, so both the iron nail and steel paper clip are attracted. Option A is the most common wrong answer because students often assume all metals are magnetic, when in fact only those containing iron, nickel, or cobalt are.

questions.title: Earth's Layers
questions.prompt: Scientists cannot dig a hole all the way to the centre of the Earth. How do scientists know what the inside of Earth is made of?

options.A: By collecting rocks from the ocean floor, which are close enough to the Earth's core to give direct samples
options.B: By studying how earthquake waves travel through the Earth at different speeds and directions, which reveals different layers
options.C: By measuring the temperature of volcanoes, which shows exactly how hot each layer of Earth must be
options.D: By calculating how long it takes rocks on the surface to cool down, which tells scientists what is below them

questions.explanation: Seismic waves from earthquakes travel through the Earth's interior and change speed or bend when they pass through materials of different densities — scientists use seismographs worldwide to map how waves travel and deduce the properties of Earth's layers. Option A is a plausible distractor because deep ocean drilling does reach the upper crust, but ocean floor rocks are nowhere near the core and do not give direct information about the mantle or core.

questions.title: Animal Classification
questions.prompt: A student is classifying a bat, a shark, a frog, and an eagle. She wants to group together all animals that are warm-blooded. Which two animals belong in her warm-blooded group?

options.A: The shark and the frog, because both live near water and regulate temperature through their environment
options.B: The bat and the eagle, because both are vertebrates that maintain a constant internal body temperature
options.C: The frog and the eagle, because amphibians and birds both live partly in water and partly on land
options.D: The bat and the frog, because both are small animals that use less energy and therefore stay warmer

questions.explanation: Warm-blooded animals (endotherms) maintain a constant internal body temperature regardless of the environment — this includes mammals (bat) and birds (eagle). Sharks are fish (cold-blooded) and frogs are amphibians (cold-blooded), meaning they rely on external heat sources. Option C is a strong distractor because eagles do belong in the warm-blooded group, but frogs are cold-blooded amphibians and do not.

questions.title: Fair Testing in Science
questions.prompt: Two students want to test which paper towel brand absorbs the most water. Student A dips each towel for 5 seconds. Student B uses a different size of towel for each brand. Which student is running a fairer test, and what variable must be kept the same?

options.A: Student B is fairer because using different towel sizes tests each brand under its natural conditions
options.B: Student A is fairer because keeping the dipping time the same means the only difference is the towel brand itself
options.C: Student A is fairer, but the time kept the same is not really an important variable — only the water amount matters
options.D: Both tests are equally fair because neither student changed the type of water used

questions.explanation: A fair test changes only one variable (the towel brand) and keeps all others constant, including dipping time, towel size, and water amount — Student A does this by keeping time fixed. Student B's test is unfair because different towel sizes mean a larger towel naturally absorbs more water regardless of brand quality, making it impossible to know if absorption differences are due to brand or size.

questions.title: Sun and Daytime
questions.prompt: A student says: 'The Sun moves across the sky from east to west each day because it orbits around the Earth.' What is the correct explanation for why the Sun appears to move across the sky?

options.A: The Sun does orbit Earth, but it moves from west to east, not east to west
options.B: The Earth rotates on its own axis from west to east, making the Sun appear to move from east to west relative to us
options.C: The Earth orbits the Sun in a circle, and this orbital movement makes the Sun look like it crosses the sky each day
options.D: The Moon's gravitational pull causes the Sun to shift position across the sky as the day progresses

questions.explanation: The apparent daily motion of the Sun is caused by Earth rotating on its axis once every 24 hours — since Earth spins west to east, the Sun appears to rise in the east and set in the west from our perspective on the surface. Option C is a strong distractor because Earth does orbit the Sun, but this orbital motion takes one year and causes seasonal changes, not the daily east-to-west movement of the Sun.

questions.title: Density and Floating
questions.prompt: A solid steel ship floats on water, but a small solid steel coin sinks. A student says this proves steel always floats when it is made into a large enough object. Evaluate this reasoning.

options.A: Correct — large steel objects always float because their weight spreads over a bigger area of water
options.B: Incorrect — the ship floats because its hollow shape means the overall density of the ship-plus-air is less than water, not because of its size alone
options.C: Incorrect — ships float because steel becomes less dense when it is heated in the ship-building process
options.D: Correct — larger objects always displace more water, and displacing more water always causes floating

questions.explanation: A ship floats because it is hollow and contains air — the combined density of the steel hull plus the large volume of trapped air is less than the density of water. A solid steel ship of any size would sink because solid steel has a density of about 8 g/cm³, much greater than water's 1 g/cm³. Option D is a strong distractor because ships do displace more water, but the key factor is whether the average density is less than water, not simply the amount of water displaced.

questions.title: Inherited and Learned Traits
questions.prompt: A student lists traits of her dog: brown fur, the ability to sit on command, black nose, and fear of thunder. Which two traits are most likely inherited from the dog's parents rather than learned?

options.A: Sitting on command and fear of thunder, because both are responses the dog has practised
options.B: Brown fur and black nose, because physical features like coat colour and body structure are passed on through genes
options.C: Brown fur and fear of thunder, because colour and emotions are both controlled by genes
options.D: Black nose and sitting on command, because physical features and trained behaviours are both inherited

questions.explanation: Physical characteristics like fur colour and nose colour are determined by genes inherited from parents, while behaviours like obeying commands are learned through training and experience. Fear of thunder can be partially instinctive but is strongly influenced by experience, making the two clearly inherited traits the physical ones. Option C is the top distractor because students may believe emotional responses are purely genetic, but fear of thunder is significantly shaped by individual experience.

questions.title: Air and Weather Patterns
questions.prompt: A student notices that clouds form over mountains even on days when the sky is clear over nearby flat land. What is the most likely reason clouds form more easily over mountains?

options.A: Mountains attract moisture from the ground below them because rock absorbs and releases water vapour upward
options.B: Air is forced upward by mountain slopes, cools as it rises, and water vapour condenses into cloud droplets
options.C: Mountains are colder than flat land, so water in the air freezes directly onto the mountain and forms clouds
options.D: The wind blows faster over mountains, and faster-moving air always contains more water vapour that quickly becomes clouds

questions.explanation: When moist air is pushed upward over a mountain (orographic lifting), it expands and cools — when the temperature drops to the dew point, water vapour condenses into tiny water droplets, forming clouds. This is called orographic cloud formation. Option C is a strong distractor because mountains are indeed colder at higher elevations, but cloud formation requires condensation from rising and cooling air, not freezing onto the mountain surface.

questions.title: Food Chains and Energy
questions.prompt: In a grassland food chain — grass → grasshopper → frog → hawk — what happens to most of the energy that the grasshopper gets from eating grass?

options.A: It is stored completely in the grasshopper's body for the frog to use.
options.B: It is lost as heat and used for the grasshopper's life processes, so only a small fraction passes to the frog.
options.C: It is transferred in full to the frog when the grasshopper is eaten.
options.D: It is absorbed back into the soil when the grasshopper moves.

questions.explanation: Only about 10% of energy at one trophic level passes to the next; the rest is used for movement, growth, and released as heat during respiration. Option A is wrong because energy is not stored completely — much is lost during the grasshopper's own life processes before it is ever eaten.

questions.title: States of Matter Changes
questions.prompt: When water vapour in the air touches a cold glass of juice, tiny water droplets form on the outside of the glass. What change of state is happening, and what causes it?

options.A: Evaporation — the juice heats the air and turns liquid water into gas.
options.B: Freezing — the cold glass turns water vapour directly into ice crystals.
options.C: Condensation — the cold glass cools the water vapour until it loses enough energy to become liquid.
options.D: Melting — ice inside the glass melts and leaks through to the outside surface.

questions.explanation: Condensation occurs when a gas loses enough thermal energy to change into a liquid; the cold surface of the glass removes heat from nearby water vapour, causing it to condense into liquid droplets. Option B is wrong because freezing requires temperatures at or below 0 °C, which a cold drink glass does not normally reach.

questions.title: Photosynthesis Inputs
questions.prompt: A student says: 'Plants make their own food using only water and sunlight.' Identify the error in this statement.

options.A: Plants do not use sunlight; they use heat from the soil instead.
options.B: The student has left out carbon dioxide, which plants also take in through their leaves to make food.
options.C: Plants do not use water; they absorb dissolved sugars directly from the soil.
options.D: The student has left out oxygen, which plants must absorb from the air to produce food.

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis requires water, sunlight, AND carbon dioxide — plants absorb CO₂ through tiny pores called stomata in their leaves. Option D is wrong because oxygen is a product of photosynthesis, not an input required to make food.

questions.title: Gravity and Falling Objects
questions.prompt: A student drops a golf ball and a tennis ball from the same height at exactly the same time. Both balls have the same size but slightly different masses. Ignoring air resistance, which ball hits the ground first?

options.A: The golf ball, because it is heavier and gravity pulls harder on heavier objects.
options.B: The tennis ball, because it is lighter and falls more freely.
options.C: They hit the ground at the same time, because gravity accelerates all objects equally regardless of mass.
options.D: It depends on which ball the student releases a fraction of a second earlier.

questions.explanation: Gravity accelerates all objects at the same rate (9.8 m/s² on Earth) regardless of their mass, so both balls reach the ground simultaneously when air resistance is ignored — a principle demonstrated by Galileo. Option A is a common misconception; while gravity exerts more force on a heavier object, that object also has more inertia, so the acceleration remains the same.

questions.title: Rock Cycle Processes
questions.prompt: Molten rock (magma) cools and hardens deep inside the Earth over millions of years, forming large crystals. What type of rock is produced, and why are the crystals large?

options.A: Sedimentary rock — layers of sediment are compressed slowly, allowing crystals to grow.
options.B: Metamorphic rock — heat and pressure cause minerals to recrystallise into large grains.
options.C: Igneous rock — slow cooling underground gives minerals a long time to arrange into large crystals.
options.D: Igneous rock — fast cooling traps minerals quickly, forcing them to grow large to release heat.

questions.explanation: Intrusive igneous rocks like granite form when magma cools very slowly underground; slow cooling gives mineral atoms time to move and join growing crystals, resulting in large, visible crystals. Option D is wrong because fast cooling actually produces small crystals, as seen in extrusive igneous rocks like basalt.

questions.title: Light Refraction
questions.prompt: A pencil placed in a glass of water appears bent or broken at the water's surface when viewed from the side. What scientific principle explains this observation?

options.A: Reflection — the water surface acts like a mirror and bounces light from the pencil at an angle.
options.B: Refraction — light changes speed as it moves between water and air, causing it to bend and shift the pencil's apparent position.
options.C: Diffraction — light waves spread out around the edges of the pencil inside the water.
options.D: Absorption — water absorbs some colours of light, changing how the pencil looks.

questions.explanation: Refraction occurs because light travels more slowly in water than in air; when it crosses the boundary between the two materials, it changes direction, making the submerged part of the pencil appear shifted from its real position. Option A is wrong because reflection would produce a mirror image, not a bent-pencil effect.

questions.title: Adaptation and Natural Selection
questions.prompt: In a population of beetles, some are green and some are brown. Birds eat more green beetles because green ones are easier to spot on brown soil. Over many generations, what would most likely happen to the beetle population?

options.A: Green beetles would learn to hide better, so both colours would survive equally.
options.B: All beetles would gradually turn brown by deciding to change their colour.
options.C: The proportion of brown beetles would increase because brown beetles survive longer and reproduce more.
options.D: The proportion of green beetles would increase because fewer of them are eaten each generation.

questions.explanation: Natural selection favours brown beetles because they are better camouflaged on brown soil, survive longer, and pass on their colouring to more offspring — increasing the proportion of brown beetles over generations. Option D is wrong because the question states that green beetles are eaten more, meaning fewer green beetles survive to reproduce.

questions.title: Water Cycle Stages
questions.prompt: What would most likely happen to the water cycle in a region if a large area of forest was completely cleared, removing all the trees and plants?

options.A: Evaporation would increase because bare soil heats up more and releases more water vapour.
options.B: Transpiration would drop significantly, reducing the amount of water vapour released into the atmosphere from that area.
options.C: Precipitation would increase because clouds form more easily over open land than over forests.
options.D: The water cycle would be unaffected because oceans supply all the water vapour in the atmosphere.

questions.explanation: Trees release large amounts of water vapour through transpiration; removing forests dramatically reduces this process, lowering local humidity and often reducing rainfall in that region. Option A is partially true but is not the most significant or correct change — increased bare-soil evaporation is minor compared to the loss of transpiration from an entire forest.

questions.title: Electrical Conductors
questions.prompt: A student tests several materials by placing each one between the two ends of an open circuit containing a battery and a bulb. The bulb lights up for copper wire and iron nail, but not for rubber, glass, or dry wood. What can the student correctly conclude?

options.A: Only shiny materials can conduct electricity.
options.B: All metals conduct electricity and all non-metals do not.
options.C: Metals tested (copper and iron) conduct electricity, while the non-metals tested (rubber, glass, wood) do not, but this result may not apply to all metals or all non-metals.
options.D: The bulb lit up because copper and iron are magnetic, which creates an electric current.

questions.explanation: The student can only draw conclusions about the specific materials tested; copper and iron conducted electricity, while the non-metals did not — but a careful scientist notes that not all metals conduct equally and some non-metals (like graphite) can conduct. Option B states an overly broad rule: not all non-metals are insulators (graphite is a conductor), so this conclusion goes beyond the evidence.

questions.title: Human Digestive System
questions.prompt: Which organ in the human digestive system produces bile, a substance that helps break down fats into tiny droplets so they can be digested more easily?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Pancreas
options.C: Liver
options.D: Small intestine

questions.explanation: The liver produces bile, which is stored in the gallbladder and released into the small intestine where it emulsifies fats — breaking large fat droplets into smaller ones to increase the surface area for enzymes to act on. Option B is a strong distractor because the pancreas also releases digestive juices into the small intestine, but it produces enzymes (like lipase), not bile.

questions.title: Thermal Expansion
questions.prompt: A metal lid on a glass jar is very tight and hard to open. A student runs hot water over the metal lid for a few seconds, and it becomes easy to twist off. Why does heating the lid help?

options.A: The hot water makes the metal lid softer and weaker, so it bends more easily.
options.B: Metals expand when heated; the lid expands slightly more than the glass, loosening the seal.
options.C: The water washes away rust or dirt that was holding the lid in place.
options.D: Heat causes the glass jar to shrink, creating a gap between the lid and the jar.
