options.D: The claim is correct only for carbon dioxide; other greenhouse gases such as water vapour should be increased.

questions.explanation: Without any greenhouse effect, Earth's average temperature would be approximately −18 °C instead of the current +15 °C, making complex life impossible; the problem is the enhanced greenhouse effect driven by additional CO₂, methane, and other gases from human activity. Option C is wrong because, although water vapour is the most abundant greenhouse gas, human activities significantly increase CO₂ and methane, which amplify warming and also cause more water vapour to enter the atmosphere through feedback loops.

questions.title: Gravity and Orbital Motion
questions.prompt: The International Space Station orbits Earth at about 400 km altitude. Astronauts inside appear to float weightlessly. A student claims this is because there is no gravity at that altitude. What is the most accurate counter-argument?

options.A: Gravity is completely absent above 100 km, so the astronauts float because there is truly nothing pulling them down.
options.B: Gravity at 400 km is still about 88% as strong as on Earth's surface; astronauts appear weightless because they and the station are both in continuous free fall around Earth.
options.C: The station's engines cancel out gravity exactly, creating a zero-gravity zone inside.
options.D: Weightlessness occurs because the station moves so fast that centrifugal force completely replaces gravity with an outward push.

questions.explanation: Earth's gravitational pull at 400 km altitude is approximately 8.7 m/s², very close to the 9.8 m/s² at the surface; the station and everything inside are constantly falling toward Earth but also moving sideways fast enough that they keep missing it — this is orbital motion, and the sensation is identical to free fall. Option D misuses the concept of centrifugal force; in the reference frame of physics, it is gravity providing the centripetal force for circular orbit, not centrifugal force 'replacing' gravity.

questions.title: Acid-Base Indicators
questions.prompt: A student uses red cabbage juice as an indicator. She adds it to three liquids: lemon juice (turns pink), baking soda solution (turns green), and distilled water (stays purple). What can she correctly conclude about distilled water?

options.A: Distilled water is mildly acidic because the indicator did not turn green.
options.B: Distilled water is neutral because the indicator colour remained unchanged, matching neither the acidic nor the alkaline result.
options.C: Distilled water is alkaline because it did not turn pink like the lemon juice.
options.D: No conclusion can be drawn because red cabbage juice only works accurately with fruit-based liquids.

questions.explanation: Red cabbage juice (containing anthocyanin pigments) stays purple at a neutral pH of 7, turns pink or red in acids, and turns green or yellow in alkalis; distilled water's unchanged colour is the reference point for neutrality. Option A is wrong because remaining purple indicates neither acidic nor alkaline conditions — turning pink would indicate acidity, but the indicator's colour did not change at all.

questions.title: Seed Dispersal Mechanisms
questions.prompt: A maple tree produces seeds with wing-like structures that spin as they fall. A coconut palm produces large, buoyant seeds with a hard outer shell. Compare these two dispersal strategies and explain what environmental factor each is best adapted to exploit.

options.A: Maple seeds exploit wind by creating lift and rotation to travel further from the parent tree; coconut seeds exploit water currents by floating across rivers and seas to new coastlines.
options.B: Both seeds exploit wind; the coconut's shell helps it spin in air just like the maple's wings.
options.C: Maple seeds exploit gravity to fall straight down quickly; coconuts exploit animals that crack them open and scatter the pieces.
options.D: Maple seeds exploit animal fur by sticking to passing creatures; coconuts exploit wind by rolling along the ground.

questions.explanation: The maple's wing (samara) creates autorotation in air, slowing descent and allowing wind to carry it tens of metres from the parent — an adaptation to wind dispersal; the coconut's thick, fibrous, waterproof husk traps air, making it buoyant, so ocean and river currents carry it to distant shores — an adaptation to water dispersal. Option B incorrectly attributes both to wind; the coconut is far too heavy and lacks aerodynamic structure to be wind-dispersed effectively.

questions.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
questions.prompt: A book sits motionless on a table. A student says the forces on the book are unbalanced because gravity is pulling it down. What is wrong with this analysis, and what is actually true about the forces?

options.A: The student is correct; gravity is the only force, and objects always accelerate downward even when on a surface.
options.B: The student is wrong; the table exerts an upward normal force equal to the weight of the book, so the forces are balanced and the net force is zero.
options.C: The student is wrong; on Earth, gravity does not act on objects that are already resting on a surface.
options.D: The student is partially right; gravity pulls down and friction from the table surface pushes sideways, balancing the forces.

questions.explanation: Newton's third law and the concept of normal force mean the table pushes upward on the book with a force exactly equal to the book's weight (gravity downward); these two forces are balanced, giving a net force of zero, which is why the stationary book remains stationary (Newton's first law). Option D is wrong because friction acts parallel to a surface to oppose sliding motion — a stationary book on a flat table has no sideways tendency to slide, so friction is not the relevant balancing force; the normal (perpendicular) force is.

questions.title: Rock Cycle and Igneous Rocks
questions.prompt: Granite is an igneous rock found deep underground, while basalt is also igneous but is common at Earth's surface after volcanic eruptions. Both form from magma, yet granite has large visible crystals and basalt has very small ones. What best explains this difference?

options.A: Granite forms from hotter magma than basalt, and hotter magma always produces larger crystals regardless of cooling speed.
options.B: Basalt contains fewer minerals than granite, so there is less material available to form large crystals.
options.C: Granite cools slowly deep underground, giving mineral crystals time to grow large; basalt cools rapidly at the surface, leaving little time for crystal growth.
options.D: Granite is compressed by overlying rock, which forces minerals to fuse into large visible grains, unlike basalt at the surface.

questions.explanation: Crystal size in igneous rocks is directly related to the rate of cooling: slow cooling deep underground (intrusive/plutonic formation) allows atoms to organise into large crystals over thousands of years, producing coarse-grained granite; rapid cooling at the surface (extrusive formation) freezes the structure quickly, producing fine-grained basalt. Option A is wrong because it is the rate of cooling, not the initial temperature of the magma, that determines crystal size.

questions.title: Human Digestive System
questions.prompt: A student traces the journey of a piece of bread through the digestive system. She correctly identifies the mouth, stomach, and large intestine but skips the small intestine, saying it 'just passes food along.' Identify the key error in her account.

options.A: The small intestine is the primary site where most nutrients — including glucose from starch — are absorbed into the bloodstream; skipping it omits the most important absorption step.
options.B: The small intestine is where all chewing and mechanical breakdown of food occurs, not just digestion in the mouth.
options.C: The small intestine produces stomach acid, so skipping it means ignoring where protein digestion begins.
options.D: The small intestine stores faeces before they are expelled, so skipping it omits the waste storage function.

questions.explanation: The small intestine, despite its name, is about 6–7 metres long in adults and is the major site of both chemical digestion and nutrient absorption — its lining has millions of villi that absorb glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids directly into the blood and lymph. Option D is wrong because faeces storage is the function of the large intestine (particularly the rectum), not the small intestine.

questions.title: Density and Floating Objects
questions.prompt: A solid steel ball sinks in water, yet a steel ship floats. A student claims the ship floats because steel becomes less dense when shaped into a ship. Evaluate this claim scientifically.

options.A: The claim is correct; the process of shaping steel into thin sheets changes its atomic structure, lowering its density.
options.B: The claim is incorrect; the steel itself remains the same density, but the ship's hollow shape means the average density of the whole ship (steel plus enclosed air) is less than water, allowing it to float.
options.C: The claim is incorrect; ships float because water molecules bond to the steel surface, pushing the ship upward with enough force to overcome gravity.
options.D: The claim is partially correct; ships float because salt in seawater increases buoyancy enough to support even solid steel objects of any shape.

questions.explanation: The density of steel itself does not change when shaped — it is always about 7.8 g/cm³, far denser than water; however, a hollow ship encloses a large volume of air (density ~0.001 g/cm³), so the average density of the entire vessel is less than 1 g/cm³, satisfying Archimedes' principle and allowing it to float. Option D is wrong because, while saltwater is denser than freshwater and provides slightly more buoyancy, solid steel objects still sink in seawater — shape and enclosed air are the determining factors.

questions.title: Carbon Cycle and Decomposition
questions.prompt: When a tree dies and falls in a forest, its carbon does not simply disappear. Describe the most important process that returns the carbon from the dead wood back to the atmosphere, and identify which organisms are responsible.

options.A: Photosynthesis by surrounding plants absorbs the carbon directly from the dead wood through root contact.
options.B: Decomposers such as fungi and bacteria break down the organic compounds in the wood through respiration, releasing carbon dioxide back into the atmosphere.
options.C: Evaporation causes carbon compounds to turn into water vapour, which carries the carbon into clouds.
options.D: Herbivores eat the dead wood, digest it, and release the carbon as methane through their digestive processes.

questions.explanation: Decomposers — primarily fungi and bacteria — secrete enzymes that break down complex organic molecules in dead wood; the organisms then use cellular respiration to extract energy, releasing CO₂ as a by-product, which re-enters the atmosphere and completes the carbon cycle. Option A is wrong because plants absorb CO₂ gas through their leaves via photosynthesis, not carbon compounds directly from solid dead matter through roots.

questions.title: Sound Waves and Medium
questions.prompt: An astronaut outside the International Space Station cannot hear her colleague who is also outside, even though both are shouting. Meanwhile, she can hear Mission Control through her radio. Which explanation is most scientifically precise?

options.A: Sound waves require a medium of particles to travel through; space is a near-perfect vacuum with too few particles to transmit the vibrations, while radio waves are electromagnetic and travel without a medium.
options.B: The helmets absorb all sound vibrations before they can leave the suit, but radios bypass this by using Bluetooth signals.
options.C: Shouting produces low-frequency waves that cannot travel in cold temperatures, whereas radio uses high-frequency waves unaffected by cold.
options.D: Sound travels in space but is too spread out over large distances; the astronauts are simply too far apart even when standing near each other.

questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave that needs a material medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to propagate; space is essentially a vacuum, so sound vibrations have no particles to pass through. Radio waves are electromagnetic radiation — part of the same family as light — and can travel through a vacuum at the speed of light, making wireless communication in space possible. Option D is wrong because even centimetres apart in space, the near-total absence of particles means sound simply cannot propagate, regardless of distance.

questions.title: Adaptation and Extreme Cold
questions.prompt: Arctic foxes have small, rounded ears, short legs, and a thick double-layered fur coat. A student argues that the fur coat is the only adaptation that matters for surviving cold. What important functional role do the small ears and short legs play that the student is overlooking?

options.A: Small ears improve hearing in snowy conditions, helping the fox hunt prey under the snow more effectively than large ears would.
options.B: Small ears and short legs reduce the total surface area of the body relative to its volume, which minimises heat loss to the cold environment.
options.C: Short legs make the fox lower to the ground, where temperatures are slightly warmer because heat rises away from the snow surface.
options.D: Small ears reduce wind resistance when running across open tundra, allowing the fox to chase prey more efficiently.

questions.explanation: According to Bergmann's and Allen's rules, animals in cold climates tend to have compact bodies with small appendages to reduce the surface-area-to-volume ratio; a lower ratio means less body surface through which heat can escape, conserving core temperature. Option A is partially true — reduced ear size does affect hearing — but this is not the primary evolutionary driver of small ears in cold-climate animals; thermoregulation is the dominant selective pressure.

questions.title: Mixtures and Separation Methods
questions.prompt: A student needs to separate a mixture of sand, salt, and iron filings. She plans to use only a magnet. A classmate says she needs at least three steps to fully separate all three components. Who is correct, and what is the most logical sequence?

options.A: The student is correct; a magnet alone pulls the iron filings out and the sand and salt separate automatically because they have different colours.
options.B: The classmate is correct: use a magnet to remove iron filings, then dissolve the remaining mixture in water and filter to collect sand, then evaporate the water to recover salt.
options.C: The classmate is correct: filter the mixture first to collect sand, then use a magnet on the filtrate to collect iron filings, then evaporate to get salt.
options.D: The student is correct; adding water dissolves everything including sand, so a single evaporation step leaves all three components separated in layers.

questions.explanation: Three steps are needed: (1) magnet removes iron filings (magnetically attracted); (2) adding water dissolves salt but not sand, and filtering separates the insoluble sand; (3) evaporating the saltwater solution recovers the salt — each step exploits a different physical property. Option C is wrong because filtering a dry mixture does not work — sand and iron filings are both solid particulates; a filter separates solids from liquids, not two different solids from each other.

questions.title: Soil Formation and Weathering
questions.prompt: A scientist studying a rocky mountainside finds that the soil at the base is much deeper and richer than the thin, rocky layer near the summit. What combination of processes best explains this difference?

options.A: Wind blows soil particles downward over time, and water carries dissolved minerals down the slope; the summit loses material while the base accumulates it, and biological activity enriches the deeper deposits further.
options.B: The base rock is softer than the summit rock, so it weathers faster and produces more soil in the same amount of time.
options.C: More sunlight reaches the summit, drying out and destroying soil particles before they can accumulate.
options.D: Trees grow only at the base and their roots chemically dissolve the rock beneath them, creating soil rapidly.

questions.explanation: Gravity and water transport eroded particles downslope over long periods (erosion and deposition), so material that weathers from higher elevations accumulates at the base; greater moisture, temperature stability, and biological activity (decomposers, plant roots) at lower elevations also speed up soil formation and organic enrichment. Option B is wrong because the difference in soil depth is not primarily due to rock hardness — the dominant factors are the physical transport of material downhill and the longer residence time of soil at the base.

questions.title: Pulse Rate and Exercise
questions.prompt: A student measures her resting pulse at 72 beats per minute. After running for 3 minutes, it rises to 130 bpm. She claims her heart is working harder to make more blood. Identify the scientific inaccuracy and provide the correct explanation.

options.A: She is wrong that blood volume increases; the heart beats faster to circulate existing blood more quickly, delivering oxygen and glucose to muscles and removing carbon dioxide faster.
options.B: She is correct; the body produces new blood cells within minutes of exercise beginning, and the heart speeds up to pump this extra blood.
options.C: She is wrong; the heart does not speed up during exercise — only breathing rate increases, and the pulse measurement was incorrect.
options.D: She is partially right; the heart makes more plasma during exercise but not red blood cells, so her explanation is half correct.

questions.explanation: During exercise, muscle cells respire faster, consuming oxygen and glucose and producing carbon dioxide more rapidly; the heart increases its rate to circulate the existing blood volume faster, delivering more oxygen and removing more CO₂ per minute — the total volume of blood in the body does not increase during a 3-minute run. Option B is wrong because producing new blood cells (haematopoiesis) takes days in the bone marrow, not minutes during a short exercise bout.

questions.title: Moon Phases Explained
questions.prompt: A student draws the Moon's phases and labels the 'new moon' as occurring when Earth's shadow blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon. Identify the error in this explanation.

options.A: The error is that a new moon occurs when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; from Earth we see only the Moon's unlit side because the lit face points toward the Sun, away from us — not because of Earth's shadow.
options.B: The error is minor; Earth's shadow does cause the new moon, but only during the winter months when the Sun is lower in the sky.
options.C: The error is that Earth's shadow causes a lunar eclipse, not the new moon; but the student's description of the new moon's position is still correct.
options.D: There is no error; the new moon occurs whenever Earth's shadow fully covers the Moon's surface from any viewer's perspective.

questions.explanation: A new moon occurs when the Moon is positioned between Earth and the Sun (conjunction); sunlight illuminates the side of the Moon facing the Sun, which faces away from Earth, so we see the unlit hemisphere — no shadow from Earth is involved. Earth's shadow causes a lunar eclipse, which only happens during a full moon when Earth is between the Sun and Moon; the student has confused two completely different phenomena.

questions.title: Reversible and Irreversible Changes
questions.prompt: A student lists these changes: melting ice, burning wood, dissolving sugar in water, and baking a cake. She claims all four are irreversible because something new is formed each time. How many of her four examples are actually reversible, and which are they?

options.A: None are reversible; once any substance changes form, energy is permanently lost and it cannot return to its original state.
options.B: Two are reversible: melting ice (re-freeze the water) and dissolving sugar (evaporate the water to recover the sugar); burning wood and baking a cake are irreversible chemical changes.
options.C: Three are reversible: melting ice, dissolving sugar, and baking a cake; only burning wood is truly irreversible because it produces ash.
options.D: One is reversible: melting ice only; dissolving sugar is irreversible because the sugar disappears and cannot be recovered.

questions.explanation: Melting ice is a physical change reversed by freezing, and dissolving sugar is a physical change reversed by evaporating the solvent to crystallise the sugar again; both involve no new substances. Burning wood and baking a cake are irreversible chemical changes because new substances are formed (gases, carbon, new compounds in cake batter) that cannot practically be converted back to the original materials.

questions.title: Food Web Energy Loss
questions.prompt: In a meadow food chain, grass stores 10,000 units of energy. Only about 1,000 units reach the rabbits that eat the grass, and only about 100 units reach the foxes that eat the rabbits. A student claims the 'lost' energy is destroyed. What actually happens to most of the energy at each step?

options.A: It is stored permanently in the bones and tissues of the organism that was eaten
options.B: It is released as heat during life processes such as movement, digestion, and keeping warm
options.C: It is passed into the soil when organisms excrete waste and becomes unavailable forever
options.D: It is converted into light energy and radiated back into the atmosphere

questions.explanation: At each trophic level, organisms use most of their energy for metabolic processes—movement, digestion, thermoregulation—releasing it as heat, which disperses into the environment. Option C is wrong because waste energy in soil is actually used by decomposers and re-enters the cycle rather than disappearing forever.

questions.title: Water Cycle Condensation
questions.prompt: On a cold morning, water droplets appear on the outside of a glass filled with an icy drink, even though the glass has no holes. Which explanation is most scientifically accurate for why this happens?

options.A: Water seeps slowly through the microscopic pores in the glass from the inside to the outside
options.B: The cold surface of the glass cools the surrounding air, causing water vapour already in the air to change into liquid droplets
options.C: The icy drink produces water molecules that travel through the air and stick to the outside of the glass
options.D: Cold air contains more water than warm air, so the extra water is pushed out onto the nearest cold surface

questions.explanation: Water vapour is always present in air; when it contacts a cold surface it loses enough energy to condense back into liquid—this is condensation, the same process that forms clouds. Option A is wrong because standard drinking glasses are not porous enough to allow liquid water to seep through.

questions.title: Natural Selection Camouflage
questions.prompt: A population of moths lives on trees covered in pale lichen. Most moths are pale, but a few are dark. After a factory nearby covers the trees in dark soot, scientists observe that dark moths become far more common over several generations. Which explanation best describes the mechanism behind this change?

options.A: Individual pale moths gradually changed their own colour to match the sooty trees during their lifetimes
options.B: The soot chemicals caused all moths to produce more dark pigment within a single generation
options.C: Dark moths survived and reproduced more because they were better camouflaged from predators on dark trees, passing their dark colouring to offspring
options.D: Pale moths migrated away from the polluted area, leaving only dark moths behind regardless of any survival advantage

questions.explanation: Natural selection works because dark moths had a survival advantage—better camouflage—so they lived longer and produced more offspring who inherited the dark colouring, increasing the proportion of dark moths across generations. Option A describes Lamarckian inheritance, which is incorrect; individual organisms cannot change their inherited traits through need alone.

questions.title: Dissolved Oxygen in Water
questions.prompt: A student notices that fish in a garden pond die in large numbers during a very hot summer, even though the pond still contains plenty of water. Identify the most likely scientific cause of the fish deaths.

options.A: Warmer water holds less dissolved oxygen, so the fish cannot extract enough oxygen to survive
options.B: Hot sunlight directly damages the gills of fish swimming near the surface of the pond
options.C: High temperatures cause the water to become more acidic, which is toxic to most fish species
options.D: Fish require cooler water to digest food, so they starve when temperatures rise in summer

questions.explanation: Gases dissolve less easily in warmer water—as temperature rises, dissolved oxygen levels drop, and fish (which extract oxygen through their gills) can suffocate even in a full pond. Option C is a plausible distractor but incorrect here; while pollution can acidify water, simple heating does not significantly lower pH in a garden pond.

questions.title: Separating Mixtures Methods
questions.prompt: A student has a mixture of salt, sand, and iron filings. She wants to separate all three substances. Which sequence of methods would successfully separate all three components?

options.A: Use a magnet to remove iron filings, dissolve the rest in water, then filter to collect sand and evaporate to collect salt
options.B: Filter the whole mixture through paper to collect sand and iron filings together, then evaporate to collect salt
options.C: Dissolve the whole mixture in water, filter to collect sand, then use a magnet on the filtrate to collect iron filings
options.D: Evaporate the mixture first to remove salt, then use a magnet on the remaining sand and iron filings

questions.explanation: Iron filings are magnetic so a magnet removes them first; salt dissolves in water but sand does not, so filtering separates the sand, and then evaporating the salt solution recovers the salt—three distinct and appropriate techniques for each material's properties. Option C fails because iron filings do not dissolve in water and a magnet cannot act on them while they are suspended in liquid at this scale.

questions.title: Fault Lines and Earthquakes
questions.prompt: Earth's crust is made of large tectonic plates that move a few centimetres each year. A student claims that earthquakes only happen at the edges where two plates collide head-on. Evaluate this claim.

options.A: The claim is correct; earthquakes only occur when plates push directly into each other with great force
options.B: The claim is partly correct; earthquakes can also occur where plates move apart, but not where they slide sideways past each other
options.C: The claim is incorrect; earthquakes can occur where plates collide, pull apart, or slide sideways, and occasionally within a plate near old fault lines
options.D: The claim is incorrect; earthquakes have nothing to do with plate boundaries and instead result from volcanic activity beneath the ocean floor

questions.explanation: Seismic activity occurs at all three types of plate boundaries—convergent, divergent, and transform (sideways)—and intraplate earthquakes happen along ancient fault lines within plates, such as the New Madrid Seismic Zone in the USA. Option B is wrong because transform boundaries like the San Andreas Fault in California are among the most earthquake-prone regions on Earth.

questions.title: Photosynthesis Limiting Factors
questions.prompt: A farmer grows tomatoes in a large greenhouse and wants to maximise plant growth. She increases the carbon dioxide level and the amount of light, but growth stops improving beyond a certain point. What is the most likely reason growth does not continue to increase?

options.A: Too much carbon dioxide becomes toxic to the plant and begins to slow photosynthesis
options.B: Another factor, such as temperature or water supply, is now limiting the rate of photosynthesis
options.C: Once a plant receives enough light, extra carbon dioxide has no further chemical role in photosynthesis
options.D: The chloroplasts in the leaves become saturated with colour and can no longer absorb any more light energy

questions.explanation: The concept of limiting factors means that even if you optimise light and CO₂, the slowest factor—often temperature or water—caps the overall rate of photosynthesis; you cannot increase the rate further until that bottleneck is addressed. Option A is incorrect because normal elevated CO₂ levels used in horticulture (up to ~1,000–1,500 ppm) are not toxic to plants.

questions.title: Thermal Expansion of Materials
questions.prompt: Engineers building a long steel railway leave small gaps between sections of track. A student says this is a waste of material and the gaps should be filled with steel to make the track stronger. What would actually happen if the gaps were completely filled?

options.A: Nothing significant; steel is rigid enough that temperature changes would not affect its length at railway scales
options.B: The track would become slightly shorter in summer as the steel compressed under the weight of trains
options.C: On hot days the steel would expand, and with no room to expand the track could buckle and bend dangerously
options.D: The extra steel would conduct electricity from lightning strikes along the track, causing safety problems

questions.explanation: Steel expands when heated; a long track with no expansion gaps can generate enormous compressive forces on hot days, causing it to buckle sideways—a phenomenon called 'sun kink' that has caused real derailments. Option A is wrong because the thermal expansion of steel is significant over long distances; a 1 km steel rail can expand by about 12 cm between winter and summer.

questions.title: Greenhouse Effect Mechanism
questions.prompt: A student explains the greenhouse effect by saying: 'Greenhouse gases act like a mirror and reflect the Sun's rays back into space before they can reach Earth's surface.' Identify the specific error in this explanation.

options.A: The error is that greenhouse gases are transparent to incoming solar radiation but absorb and re-emit the longer-wave infrared radiation leaving Earth's surface
options.B: The error is that only water vapour acts as a greenhouse gas; carbon dioxide and methane have no significant warming effect
options.C: The error is that greenhouse gases are located in the stratosphere rather than the troposphere and therefore cannot interact with sunlight
options.D: The error is that the greenhouse effect is caused by the ozone layer, not by carbon dioxide or water vapour

questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases like CO₂ and water vapour actually let most incoming shortwave solar radiation pass through, but they absorb the longer-wave infrared (heat) radiation that Earth's surface radiates outward, re-emitting some back toward Earth and warming it. Option D confuses two separate atmospheric phenomena: the ozone layer absorbs ultraviolet radiation and protects against sunburn, but it is not the primary driver of the greenhouse effect.

questions.title: Refraction of Light
questions.prompt: When a straight straw is placed in a glass of water, it appears bent or broken at the water's surface. Two students debate the cause. Student A says light travels more slowly in water than in air, causing it to change direction. Student B says the water magnifies the straw and makes it look displaced. Which student is correct, and why?

options.A: Student B, because water acts as a convex lens and magnifies objects placed inside it
options.B: Student A, because the change in speed of light as it crosses from water to air causes it to bend, shifting the apparent position of the straw
options.C: Both students are equally correct; refraction and magnification are two names for the same optical phenomenon
options.D: Neither student; the straw only appears bent because of reflections from the inner glass surface, not any property of water

questions.explanation: Refraction occurs because light slows down when entering a denser medium (water) and speeds up when it leaves—this change in speed causes the light rays to bend at the surface, making the submerged part of the straw appear shifted from its actual position. Student B's magnification explanation is incorrect; while water can produce magnification in a curved container, the bending effect here is purely due to the change in direction of light rays at the flat water–air boundary.

questions.title: Rock Cycle and Formation
questions.prompt: A geologist finds a rock sample containing clear layers of different coloured minerals with tiny fossils of sea creatures embedded in it, even though the rock was found high up in a mountain. Which type of rock is it, and what does finding it on a mountain tell us?

options.A: It is igneous rock, and finding it on a mountain shows that volcanoes once erupted at sea level there
options.B: It is metamorphic rock, and the fossils prove that extreme heat and pressure in mountains can create living organisms inside rock
options.C: It is sedimentary rock, and its presence on a mountain indicates that tectonic forces lifted what was once a seafloor to a high elevation
options.D: It is sedimentary rock formed in the mountain itself, because river sediment can flow uphill during major floods

questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form in horizontal layers on the beds of seas or lakes and are the only common rock type to contain marine fossils; their presence at high altitude, as in the Himalayas or Alps, is direct evidence of tectonic uplift—whole former seabeds being pushed upward by colliding plates. Option A is wrong because igneous rock forms from cooling magma and does not contain layered fossils of sea creatures.

questions.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
questions.prompt: A skydiver jumps from a plane. At first she accelerates downward, but after some time she reaches a constant speed called terminal velocity and stops accelerating. What must be true about the forces acting on her at terminal velocity?

options.A: Gravity has decreased to zero so no net force acts downward anymore
options.B: Air resistance has increased until it exactly equals the force of gravity, so the net force is zero
options.C: Air resistance has become greater than gravity, causing a slight upward net force that holds her at constant speed
options.D: Her mass decreases as she falls faster, reducing the effect of gravity until it matches air resistance

questions.explanation: As speed increases, air resistance increases until it equals the downward gravitational force; at that point the net force is zero and, by Newton's first law, the skydiver continues at constant velocity without further acceleration. Option C is wrong because if air resistance exceeded gravity there would be a net upward force, causing deceleration rather than constant speed.

questions.title: Cellular Respiration vs Breathing
questions.prompt: A student writes in her science notebook: 'Plants only respire at night, because during the day they photosynthesise instead.' Evaluate this statement using your knowledge of cellular respiration.

options.A: The statement is correct; plants switch between photosynthesis and respiration depending on the time of day
options.B: The statement is incorrect; plants respire continuously day and night, while photosynthesis only occurs when there is sufficient light
options.C: The statement is partly correct; plants only respire in their roots at night because their leaves are too busy photosynthesising during the day
options.D: The statement is incorrect; plants do not respire at all because they make all their own energy through photosynthesis

questions.explanation: Cellular respiration is the process by which all living cells—including plant cells—continuously break down glucose to release energy for life processes; it happens 24 hours a day in every living cell. Photosynthesis is an additional process that occurs in light, but it does not replace or pause respiration, so the student's claim confuses two separate processes.

questions.title: Acids and Indicators
questions.prompt: A student tests five liquids with universal indicator and records the following colours: red, orange, green, blue, purple. She concludes that the green liquid is neither an acid nor a base. A classmate says the green liquid might still be weakly acidic. Who is correct?

options.A: The student is correct; green on a universal indicator scale always indicates a neutral pH of exactly 7
options.B: The classmate is correct; on a universal indicator scale, green spans roughly pH 6–7, so it can include slightly acidic solutions
options.C: The classmate is correct, but only because universal indicator is unreliable and often produces the wrong colour for acidic liquids
options.D: Both are wrong; green indicates a strong base, not a neutral or acidic substance

questions.explanation: Universal indicator produces a range of colours across the pH scale; green typically covers approximately pH 6 to 7, meaning a pale green result could indicate a mildly acidic solution rather than a perfectly neutral one (pH 7 exactly appears as a brighter, neutral green). Option A is wrong because green does not exclusively represent pH 7—it covers a band of values, making the classmate's caution scientifically justified.

questions.title: Inherited vs Acquired Traits
questions.prompt: A farmer notices that a calf born to a cow that lost one of its horns in an accident is still born with two normal horns. Which scientific principle does this best demonstrate?

options.A: Mutations can occur spontaneously in any generation, so offspring may gain traits their parents never had
options.B: Acquired characteristics—physical changes caused by the environment or injury—are not stored in DNA and therefore are not inherited by offspring
options.C: Dominant traits from the father always override any traits lost by the mother during her lifetime
options.D: Animals only inherit traits from their parents at the moment of birth; injuries before birth affect the offspring but injuries after do not

questions.explanation: Inheritance is determined by DNA passed through reproductive cells (gametes); an injury to a grown cow does not alter the DNA in her eggs, so the characteristic of having two horns is still encoded and passed on. This disproves Lamarck's old idea that acquired characteristics can be inherited, a concept replaced by Mendelian genetics and our understanding of DNA.

questions.title: Electrical Conductors and Insulators
questions.prompt: A student tests several materials to see if they conduct electricity and records that graphite (pencil lead), copper wire, rubber, and salt water all conduct electricity. Her teacher says one material in her list is surprising to most students. Which material is that, and why is it surprising?

options.A: Rubber, because most students expect rubber to conduct electricity since it is used in tyres and boots
options.B: Salt water, because most students know pure water does not conduct electricity and are surprised that dissolved salt creates ions that carry charge
options.C: Copper wire, because most students expect only gold and silver to be able to conduct electricity in a simple circuit
options.D: Graphite, because most students expect all forms of carbon to be strong insulators like diamond

questions.explanation: Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon, yet graphite conducts electricity while diamond does not; this surprises students because they assume the same element behaves the same way. The reason is structural: in graphite, each carbon atom bonds to only three neighbours, leaving one free electron per atom that can move and carry charge, whereas in diamond all four electrons are locked in bonds.

questions.title: Phases of the Moon
questions.prompt: During a full moon, the Moon appears as a complete bright circle. Two weeks later it has completely disappeared from view as a new moon. A student claims the new moon occurs because Earth's shadow is blocking sunlight from reaching the Moon. Evaluate this claim.

options.A: The claim is correct; Earth's shadow causes both the new moon and lunar eclipses
options.B: The claim is incorrect; a new moon occurs when the Moon is positioned between Earth and the Sun, so its lit side faces away from us, not because of Earth's shadow
options.C: The claim is partly correct; Earth's shadow causes new moon phases, while the Moon's own shadow causes lunar eclipses
options.D: The claim is correct; during a new moon, Earth rotates so that land masses block our view of the Moon for approximately two weeks

questions.explanation: Moon phases result from our changing viewing angle of the Moon's sunlit half as it orbits Earth; during a new moon, the Moon is roughly between Earth and the Sun so we see only its unlit side. Earth's shadow only falls on the Moon during a lunar eclipse, which is a separate, much rarer event that lasts only a few hours.

questions.title: Adaptation and Competition
questions.prompt: Two species of finch live on the same island and both eat seeds. Scientists notice that over many generations, one species develops a slightly larger beak while the other develops a slightly smaller beak, even though both species originally had similar beak sizes. What process best explains this divergence?

options.A: The two species deliberately chose to eat different seeds so they would not have to compete with each other
options.B: Character displacement—competition between the species favoured individuals whose beaks were less similar to the other species, reducing overlap in diet and giving each a survival advantage
options.C: Mutation randomly caused the beak changes with no connection to competition or food availability
options.D: The larger finch species ate the smaller species' food and the smaller species evolved a smaller beak as a result of eating less

questions.explanation: Character displacement is a well-documented evolutionary phenomenon where competing species diverge in a shared trait, reducing direct competition; in this case individuals whose beaks differed most from the rival species could access different seed sizes and so had better survival and reproductive success. Option A is incorrect because evolution has no intention or planning—individual birds do not 'choose' to evolve; natural selection acts on inherited variation.

questions.title: Changing States and Particles
questions.prompt: When liquid water is heated to boiling point, it changes to water vapour. A student says the water molecules themselves change into a different type of molecule during this process. Is the student correct? What actually happens at the particle level?

options.A: The student is correct; heating breaks the hydrogen and oxygen atoms apart, creating a different molecule
options.B: The student is incorrect; the water molecules remain H₂O but gain enough energy to overcome the forces holding them close together, spreading far apart as a gas
options.C: The student is partly correct; half the molecules break apart into hydrogen and oxygen, while the other half remain as water vapour
options.D: The student is incorrect; at boiling point, water molecules shrink in size to become vapour particles, which is why steam is invisible

questions.explanation: A physical change of state does not alter chemical composition—water molecules (H₂O) remain intact during evaporation and boiling; what changes is the spacing and movement of molecules as they gain kinetic energy and overcome intermolecular attractions. Breaking water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen requires electrolysis or very high temperature decomposition, not simply boiling.

questions.title: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Stability
questions.prompt: Scientists compare two grassland ecosystems: one with 40 different plant and animal species and one with only 8 species. When a severe drought strikes both grasslands, the 40-species ecosystem recovers much faster. What is the most likely scientific reason for this difference in recovery?

options.A: Ecosystems with more species are always located in areas with better soil and rainfall, which helps them recover faster
options.B: In a more biodiverse ecosystem, there are more species filling each role, so if one species is lost another can perform its function and maintain the system
options.C: Having more species means each individual organism competes less for water, so every organism survives a drought more easily
options.D: More species means more total biomass in the ecosystem, so it has more stored energy to 'wait out' a drought event

questions.explanation: Higher biodiversity provides functional redundancy—multiple species can perform similar ecological roles (pollination, seed dispersal, decomposition), so if a drought eliminates one species, others with similar functions prevent the system from collapsing. Option C is misleading; having more species actually means more competition for the same water, not less.

questions.title: Sound Waves and Medium
questions.prompt: An astronaut outside a space station hammers a metal bolt. A colleague standing a metre away outside also in space cannot hear the hammering, but an astronaut inside the station who is touching the station's metal wall can hear a faint sound. What does this experiment reveal about how sound travels?

options.A: Sound travels only through air and the inside astronaut hears it because the station is filled with air carrying the vibrations
options.B: Sound requires a medium with particles to travel through; it cannot travel through the vacuum of space but can travel through the solid metal of the station wall
options.C: Sound travels faster in vacuum than in solids, so the outside astronaut hears the sound before it reaches the inside astronaut
options.D: The outside astronaut cannot hear because her helmet blocks all sound waves, while the inside astronaut has no helmet

questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave that needs particles to vibrate and pass energy along; in the vacuum of outer space there are almost no particles, so sound cannot propagate between the two outside astronauts, but the vibrations do travel through the solid metal molecules of the station wall to reach the inside astronaut's air-filled environment. Option A is partially true but incomplete—the key scientific point is that sound travels through the solid metal, not just the air inside the station.

questions.title: Scientific Method Evaluation
questions.prompt: A student investigates whether plants grow faster with classical music or with no music. She uses 10 identical bean seedlings, plays classical music to 5 of them for 2 hours each day in a sunny windowsill, and keeps the other 5 in a dark cupboard in silence. After 4 weeks, the music group has grown significantly taller. She concludes that music causes faster plant growth. Identify the most significant flaw in her experimental design.

options.A: She should have used more than two types of music to make the experiment more thorough
options.B: The experiment changed two variables at once—the music group had both music and sunlight while the control group had neither, so the growth difference could be caused by light rather than music
options.C: She measured the plants after too long a period; plant growth experiments should only run for one week to be reliable
options.D: Using only bean seedlings makes the experiment invalid because different plant species would need to be tested to draw any conclusion

questions.explanation: A fair test requires changing only one independent variable at a time; this student changed both the presence of music and the presence of light simultaneously, making it impossible to determine which factor caused the increased growth—sunlight alone is well-known to dramatically accelerate plant growth. Option D is a distractor; while testing multiple species would strengthen the conclusion, it is not the most critical flaw—the confounded variables problem is far more fundamental.

questions.title: Photosynthesis Inputs and Outputs
questions.prompt: A student covers all the leaves of a healthy plant with aluminium foil for two weeks, ensuring the roots still receive water. Which outcome would you most expect to observe, and why?

options.A: The plant grows faster because energy is conserved inside the covered leaves
options.B: The plant wilts and may die because it cannot produce glucose through photosynthesis
options.C: The plant survives normally because it absorbs nutrients through its roots instead
options.D: The plant stores extra water in its stem since transpiration is blocked

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis requires light to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose; without light, the plant cannot manufacture food and will deplete its energy reserves, causing wilting and eventual death. Option C is the top distractor — roots absorb minerals and water, not glucose or chemical energy, so root function alone cannot sustain the plant.

questions.title: Particle Model of Gases
questions.prompt: A sealed metal canister of gas is placed near a heat source and its temperature rises. Using the particle model, what happens to the pressure inside the canister?

options.A: Pressure decreases because the gas particles spread further apart and collide less often
options.B: Pressure stays the same because the canister is sealed and no gas escapes
options.C: Pressure increases because particles move faster and hit the walls more frequently and forcefully
options.D: Pressure increases because new gas particles are created when heat energy is added

questions.explanation: Heating a gas increases the kinetic energy of its particles, so they move faster, collide with the container walls more often and with greater force — this is the microscopic definition of increased pressure. Option A is incorrect because in a fixed volume the number of collisions actually increases with temperature, not decreases.

questions.title: Natural Selection Mechanism
questions.prompt: In a population of beetles, individuals with darker colouring are harder for birds to spot against dark tree bark. Over many generations, the proportion of dark beetles increases. Which process best explains this change?

options.A: Mutation, because the beetles deliberately change colour to match the bark
options.B: Natural selection, because darker beetles survive longer and pass on their traits to more offspring
options.C: Genetic engineering, because the environment modifies the beetles' DNA directly
options.D: Selective breeding, because humans chose which beetles could reproduce

questions.explanation: Natural selection occurs when individuals with advantageous heritable traits survive and reproduce at higher rates, increasing the frequency of those traits in the population — exactly what is described here. Option A is wrong because mutations are random, not deliberate responses to the environment; organisms cannot choose to mutate.

questions.title: Acids and pH Scale
questions.prompt: A student tests four liquids with universal indicator and records these pH values: lemon juice = 2, milk = 6.5, baking soda solution = 9, bleach = 13. Which liquid is the strongest acid?

options.A: Bleach, because it has the highest pH value
options.B: Milk, because its pH is close to neutral
options.C: Baking soda solution, because it is above 7
options.D: Lemon juice, because it has the lowest pH value

questions.explanation: The pH scale runs from 0 to 14; lower values indicate greater acidity and higher concentration of hydrogen ions. Lemon juice at pH 2 is furthest below neutral (pH 7), making it the strongest acid listed. Bleach at pH 13 is a strong alkali, not an acid — it is the top distractor because students sometimes confuse 'extreme' on the scale with 'most acidic'.

questions.title: Food Web Energy Transfer
questions.prompt: In a grassland food web, grass is eaten by grasshoppers, which are eaten by frogs, which are eaten by hawks. A student claims that the hawk receives the same amount of energy from the grass as the grasshopper does. Evaluate this claim.

options.A: The claim is correct because energy is conserved and passes completely from one organism to the next
options.B: The claim is incorrect because the hawk receives more energy, since it is the top predator
options.C: The claim is incorrect because energy is lost at each trophic level, so the hawk receives far less energy than the grasshopper
options.D: The claim is correct because all organisms in a food web share energy equally

questions.explanation: Approximately 90% of energy is lost at each trophic level through respiration, heat, and waste, so organisms higher up the food chain receive only a small fraction of the original energy stored in producers. Option A is the top distractor — while the law of conservation of energy holds for the total system, much energy is dissipated as heat and is unavailable to the next consumer.

questions.title: States of Matter Changes
questions.prompt: When water vapour in the atmosphere cools and turns into liquid droplets, forming clouds, which change of state is occurring?

options.A: Evaporation, as water particles gain energy and move into the gas phase
options.B: Condensation, as water vapour loses energy and particles come together as liquid
options.C: Freezing, as water vapour loses energy and becomes a solid
options.D: Sublimation, as water transitions directly from gas to solid

questions.explanation: Condensation is the process by which a gas loses thermal energy and its particles slow down enough to form a liquid; this is exactly how cloud droplets form as water vapour cools at altitude. Sublimation (option D) is the top distractor — it describes gas turning directly into solid (like dry ice), but cloud formation produces liquid droplets, not ice crystals.

questions.title: Gravitational Potential Energy
questions.prompt: A 2 kg book is lifted from a desk to a shelf 1.5 m higher. Assuming no energy is wasted, which statement correctly describes the energy transformation that takes place?

options.A: Kinetic energy is converted into gravitational potential energy as the book is lifted
options.B: Chemical energy in the person's muscles is converted into gravitational potential energy stored in the book
options.C: Thermal energy from the surroundings is converted into potential energy in the book
options.D: Gravitational potential energy is converted into kinetic energy as the book rises

questions.explanation: When a person lifts an object, chemical energy stored in muscle cells (from respiration) is converted into gravitational potential energy in the object, calculated as mgh (2 × 10 × 1.5 = 30 J). Option A is the top distractor — kinetic energy does increase momentarily during the lift, but the primary and final energy transformation is from chemical to gravitational potential energy, not kinetic to potential.

questions.title: DNA and Inheritance
questions.prompt: A child has blood type O. Her father has blood type A and her mother has blood type B. A student says this is impossible because neither parent has type O blood. Is this student correct? Justify your answer.

options.A: Yes, because a child can only inherit blood types that one of the parents visibly expresses
options.B: No, because blood type O is dominant over both A and B, so it always appears
options.C: No, because both parents can carry a recessive O allele without expressing it, and the child can inherit O from both
options.D: Yes, because blood type mutations must have occurred in the child's DNA

questions.explanation: Blood type A can be genotype AO (heterozygous) and blood type B can be genotype BO; if each parent carries a recessive O allele, there is a 25% chance their child receives O from both parents, resulting in blood type OO (type O). Option A is the top distractor — it incorrectly assumes offspring can only display phenotypes visible in parents, ignoring the concept of recessive alleles.

questions.title: Refraction of Light
questions.prompt: A straw placed in a glass of water appears bent at the water's surface when viewed from the side. What causes this optical effect?

options.A: Reflection, because light bounces off the water surface back to the observer's eyes
options.B: Refraction, because light changes speed as it passes from water into air, altering its direction
options.C: Diffraction, because water molecules scatter light rays as they pass through
options.D: Absorption, because water absorbs certain wavelengths of light coming from the submerged part of the straw

questions.explanation: Refraction occurs when light travels from one medium to another of different optical density; moving from denser water into less dense air, light speeds up and bends away from the normal, making the submerged portion of the straw appear displaced. Option A is the top distractor — reflection would only explain a mirror-like image at the surface, not the apparent bending of an object below the surface.

questions.title: Carbon Cycle Processes
questions.prompt: Identify the error in this student's statement: 'When animals breathe out, carbon is permanently removed from the carbon cycle and stored in the atmosphere forever.'

options.A: The error is that animals do not release carbon; only plants release CO₂
options.B: The error is that CO₂ exhaled by animals re-enters the cycle — it can be absorbed by plants for photosynthesis or dissolved in oceans
options.C: The error is that carbon is stored in bones, not exhaled as gas
options.D: The error is that only decomposers, not animals, release carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: The carbon cycle is continuous: CO₂ exhaled by animals is taken up by plants during photosynthesis or absorbed by oceans, so carbon is cycled rather than permanently stored in the atmosphere. Option A is wrong because animals do release CO₂ through cellular respiration — respiration occurs in all living organisms, not just plants.

questions.title: Separating Mixtures
questions.prompt: A student has a mixture of sand, salt, and iron filings. She wants to collect pure salt at the end. Which sequence of separation techniques would work most effectively?

options.A: Filter the mixture, then use a magnet, then evaporate the filtrate
options.B: Use a magnet to remove iron filings, then dissolve in water and filter out sand, then evaporate to collect salt
options.C: Evaporate the mixture first, then filter, then use a magnet
options.D: Dissolve everything in water, filter, then use a magnet on the filtrate

questions.explanation: Iron filings are first removed with a magnet; adding water then dissolves the salt while the sand remains as an insoluble solid that can be filtered off; finally, evaporating the salt solution recovers the pure salt — each step exploits a different physical property. Option A is the top distractor — filtering first would not separate iron filings from sand effectively, and it assumes the mixture is already dissolved, which it is not.

questions.title: Plate Tectonics Evidence
questions.prompt: Scientists have found fossils of the same extinct land reptile, Mesosaurus, on the east coast of South America and the west coast of Africa. How does this observation support the theory of plate tectonics?

options.A: It shows that Mesosaurus could swim across the Atlantic Ocean to colonise both continents
options.B: It suggests the two continents were once joined, allowing the reptile to live across a single landmass before they separated
options.C: It proves that identical species always evolve independently on different continents
options.D: It shows that ocean currents must have carried the fossils from one continent to the other

questions.explanation: Mesosaurus was a small freshwater reptile incapable of ocean crossing; finding its fossils on two now-separated continents strongly indicates those landmasses were once connected as part of Pangaea, a key piece of evidence for continental drift. Option A is the top distractor — Mesosaurus was a freshwater animal and could not survive a saltwater ocean crossing, making independent colonisation by swimming implausible.

questions.title: Electrical Conductors and Insulators
questions.prompt: A student tests several materials by connecting them in a simple circuit with a bulb and a battery. The bulb lights up for copper wire and graphite pencil, but not for rubber or distilled water. What property do copper and graphite share that explains this?

options.A: Both are metals, which always conduct electricity due to their shiny surfaces
options.B: Both contain freely moving charged particles — delocalised electrons in copper and delocalised electrons between carbon layers in graphite
options.C: Both are solid at room temperature, and all solids conduct electricity
options.D: Both are dense materials, and density determines electrical conductivity

questions.explanation: Electrical conductivity requires freely moving charged particles; copper has a sea of delocalised electrons in its metallic structure, while graphite has electrons that can move freely between its layered carbon sheets, enabling current flow. Option A is the top distractor — graphite is a non-metal, so saying 'both are metals' is factually wrong; the conducting property arises from delocalised electrons, not from being metallic.

questions.title: Greenhouse Effect Mechanism
questions.prompt: Compare the natural greenhouse effect and the enhanced greenhouse effect. Which statement most accurately describes the key difference between them?

options.A: The natural greenhouse effect cools the planet, while the enhanced greenhouse effect warms it
options.B: Both effects are identical; 'enhanced' just means the effect is measured more precisely by scientists
options.C: The natural greenhouse effect maintains temperatures suitable for life, while the enhanced greenhouse effect results from increased greenhouse gas concentrations due to human activity, trapping more heat
options.D: The enhanced greenhouse effect is caused only by water vapour, while the natural one is caused only by CO₂

questions.explanation: The natural greenhouse effect, caused by atmospheric gases like CO₂ and water vapour, keeps Earth about 33°C warmer than it would otherwise be and is essential for life; the enhanced greenhouse effect refers to additional warming caused by elevated greenhouse gas concentrations from burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and agriculture. Option A is incorrect because the natural greenhouse effect actually warms the planet — without it, Earth's average surface temperature would be around −18°C.

questions.title: Newton's First Law
questions.prompt: A hockey puck slides across an ice rink and gradually slows to a stop. A student says this disproves Newton's First Law because the puck does not keep moving forever. Evaluate this student's reasoning.

options.A: The student is correct; Newton's First Law only applies in outer space where there is no surface
options.B: The student is incorrect; Newton's First Law states an object continues at constant velocity only if no net force acts on it — friction from the ice is an unbalanced force causing the puck to decelerate
options.C: The student is correct; the puck's own mass creates a force that slows it down over time
options.D: The student is incorrect; Newton's First Law says all moving objects must eventually stop, which is exactly what the puck does

questions.explanation: Newton's First Law states that an object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by a net external force; friction between the puck and ice is an unbalanced retarding force that causes deceleration — the law is not violated. Option A is the top distractor — Newton's laws are universal, not limited to frictionless or space environments; the law applies everywhere, including situations where friction is present.

questions.title: Cell Division and Growth
questions.prompt: Why must a cell copy its DNA completely before it divides by mitosis?

options.A: So that each new daughter cell receives a full set of genetic instructions needed to function correctly
options.B: Because DNA must be destroyed during division and new DNA is created from scratch in each daughter cell
options.C: So the cell can increase its size before splitting in half
options.D: Because RNA cannot be produced unless DNA is duplicated first in each cell cycle

questions.explanation: During mitosis, one copy of each chromosome is distributed to each daughter cell; if DNA is not fully replicated beforehand, daughter cells would receive incomplete genetic information and could not produce all necessary proteins to survive. Option D is the top distractor — while DNA is used as a template for RNA, the primary reason for DNA replication before mitosis is to ensure both daughter cells inherit a complete genome, not specifically to enable RNA production.

questions.title: Wave Properties
questions.prompt: A student observes that when she increases the frequency of a wave while keeping its wave speed constant, the wavelength decreases. Which equation correctly represents this relationship?

options.A: Wave speed = frequency + wavelength
options.B: Wavelength = frequency × wave speed
options.C: Wave speed = frequency × wavelength
options.D: Frequency = wave speed + wavelength

questions.explanation: The wave equation v = fλ (wave speed = frequency × wavelength) means that at constant speed, frequency and wavelength are inversely proportional — doubling frequency halves wavelength. Option B is the top distractor — it reverses the correct relationship, incorrectly stating wavelength equals frequency times speed, which would give the wrong unit (m²/s instead of m).

questions.title: Osmosis in Plant Cells
questions.prompt: A student places a piece of carrot in a concentrated salt solution and leaves it for 30 minutes. She notices the carrot becomes soft and flexible. What process explains this, and in which direction did water move?

options.A: Diffusion; salt particles moved into the carrot cells, making them swell
options.B: Osmosis; water moved out of the carrot cells into the more concentrated salt solution, causing the cells to lose turgor pressure
options.C: Osmosis; water moved into the carrot cells from the salt solution, making the cells swell
options.D: Active transport; the carrot cells pumped water out to maintain their internal salt concentration

questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water through a semi-permeable membrane from a region of higher water potential (low solute concentration) to lower water potential (high solute concentration); water moves from the carrot cells into the saltier solution, causing the cells to lose turgor and the carrot to become limp. Option C is the top distractor — it correctly identifies osmosis but reverses the direction of water movement; water moves toward higher solute concentration, not away from it.

questions.title: Periodic Table Trends
questions.prompt: Elements in the same group of the periodic table tend to have similar chemical properties. What is the best explanation for this pattern?

options.A: They have the same atomic mass, so their nuclei interact with other atoms in the same way
options.B: They are all solids at room temperature, which determines how they react
options.C: They have the same number of electrons in their outermost shell, which determines how they form bonds
options.D: They were discovered at the same time, so scientists classified them together based on appearance

questions.explanation: Chemical reactivity is determined by the number of electrons in the outermost (valence) shell; elements in the same group share the same number of valence electrons, giving them similar bonding behaviour and reactivity patterns. Option A is the top distractor — atomic mass increases down a group, so elements in the same group do not share the same atomic mass; it is the valence electron count, not mass, that governs chemical properties.

questions.title: Rock Cycle Processes
questions.prompt: Examine this sequence: magma cools and solidifies → rock is broken down by weathering → fragments are transported and deposited → layers are compacted and cemented. Which rock types are formed at the first and last steps, respectively?

options.A: Sedimentary rock at the first step; igneous rock at the last step
options.B: Igneous rock at the first step; sedimentary rock at the last step
options.C: Metamorphic rock at the first step; igneous rock at the last step
options.D: Igneous rock at the first step; metamorphic rock at the last step

questions.explanation: When magma cools and crystallises, igneous rock is formed (e.g. granite or basalt); when sediment particles are compacted and cemented together over time, sedimentary rock is formed (e.g. sandstone or limestone). Option D is the top distractor — metamorphic rock forms when existing rock is subjected to intense heat and pressure, which is not described in the final step of the given sequence.

questions.title: Enzymes and Temperature
questions.prompt: A student measures the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction at 10°C, 37°C, and 70°C. She finds the fastest rate at 37°C and almost no reaction at 70°C. Why is the reaction rate so low at 70°C?

options.A: At 70°C, the substrate particles move too slowly to collide with the enzyme's active site
options.B: At 70°C, the enzyme has been denatured — its active site shape has changed permanently so it can no longer bind the substrate
options.C: At 70°C, all the substrate molecules have already been used up, so there is nothing left to react
options.D: At 70°C, the enzyme becomes a solid and cannot dissolve in the reaction mixture

questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins whose function depends on the precise three-dimensional shape of their active site; at temperatures above the optimum (about 37°C for human enzymes), the high thermal energy breaks hydrogen bonds maintaining this shape — a process called denaturation — permanently preventing substrate binding. Option A is the top distractor — at higher temperatures particles actually move faster and collide more frequently, so reduced collision rate is the opposite of what occurs at 70°C.

questions.title: Conservation of Mass
questions.prompt: A student burns a piece of magnesium ribbon in air. She notices the white ash produced seems heavier than the original ribbon. A classmate claims mass has been created, violating the law of conservation of mass. Who is correct? Justify.

options.A: The classmate is correct; combustion reactions always create new matter from energy
options.B: The student is correct; the increased mass shows that the law of conservation of mass does not apply to combustion
options.C: Neither is correct; the magnesium actually loses mass because energy is released as light and heat during burning
options.D: The classmate is incorrect; the mass increase occurs because magnesium reacts with oxygen from the air, and the combined mass of magnesium plus oxygen equals the mass of the product, magnesium oxide

questions.explanation: The law of conservation of mass states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction; magnesium reacts with oxygen gas (2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO), so the product includes the mass of both magnesium and the oxygen atoms incorporated from the air, explaining the apparent mass increase. Option C is the top distractor — while energy is released as light and heat, this energy comes from chemical bond rearrangement and does not represent a significant loss of measurable mass under normal conditions.

questions.title: Biodiversity and Ecosystems
questions.prompt: A tropical rainforest has hundreds of tree species, while a pine plantation has only one. Which ecosystem is likely to be more resilient to a fungal disease that kills trees, and why?

options.A: The pine plantation, because having only one species means the fungus will run out of hosts quickly
options.B: The tropical rainforest, because high biodiversity means many species are unaffected by a disease targeting one type of tree, maintaining ecosystem function
options.C: The pine plantation, because uniform genetics makes all individuals equally resistant to disease
options.D: Both ecosystems are equally resilient because all trees perform the same ecological role

questions.explanation: High biodiversity provides ecosystem resilience because if one or a few species are wiped out by disease, many others remain to fulfil similar ecological roles — this redundancy maintains energy flow, nutrient cycling, and habitat structure. Option A is the top distractor — a single-species plantation actually provides a monoculture in which a pathogen can spread rapidly through the entire crop with no resistant species to slow it, making the plantation far more vulnerable.

questions.title: Speed and Velocity Distinction
questions.prompt: A runner completes one full lap of a 400 m circular track in 80 seconds and returns to her starting point. What are her average speed and average velocity at the end of the lap?

options.A: Average speed = 5 m/s; average velocity = 5 m/s in the direction of travel
options.B: Average speed = 0 m/s; average velocity = 0 m/s
options.C: Average speed = 5 m/s; average velocity = 0 m/s because her displacement is zero
options.D: Average speed = 0 m/s; average velocity = 5 m/s because she moved around the track

questions.explanation: Average speed is total distance divided by time (400 m ÷ 80 s = 5 m/s), a scalar quantity; average velocity is displacement divided by time, and since the runner returns to her start, her displacement is zero, making average velocity 0 m/s — this illustrates the key difference between scalar speed and vector velocity. Option A is the top distractor — it incorrectly treats velocity as equal to speed, ignoring the vector nature of velocity and the zero net displacement.

questions.title: Human Circulatory System
questions.prompt: Blood returning from the body to the heart arrives first at the right atrium and is pumped to the lungs before returning to the left side of the heart. Why must blood visit the lungs before being pumped to the rest of the body?

options.A: The lungs filter out waste bacteria from the blood before it circulates to organs
options.B: Blood needs to be warmed in the lungs to reach body temperature before circulating
options.C: Blood returning from the body is deoxygenated; the lungs replenish its oxygen and remove carbon dioxide before it is distributed to body tissues
options.D: The left side of the heart is too weak to receive blood directly from the body, so the lungs act as a pressure buffer

questions.explanation: Body cells consume oxygen and produce carbon dioxide during cellular respiration; blood returning to the heart carries low oxygen levels and high CO₂, so it must pass through the lungs for gas exchange — oxygen diffuses in and CO₂ diffuses out — before oxygenated blood is pumped through the left side to the whole body. Option A is the top distractor — while the immune system does respond to pathogens in blood, the primary function of pulmonary circulation is gas exchange, not filtration.

questions.title: Photosynthesis and Light
questions.prompt: A student places an aquatic plant in bright light and observes bubbles rising from its leaves. When she moves the plant into a dim corner, fewer bubbles appear. What gas are the bubbles most likely made of, and why does the rate decrease in dim light?

options.A: Carbon dioxide, because the plant respires more slowly in dim light
options.B: Oxygen, because less light means less photosynthesis and therefore less oxygen is produced
options.C: Nitrogen, because nitrogen is the most abundant gas released by aquatic plants
options.D: Water vapour, because transpiration slows when light intensity decreases

questions.explanation: Plants produce oxygen as a by-product of photosynthesis; light is a key reactant, so lower light intensity reduces the rate of photosynthesis and therefore oxygen output. Carbon dioxide is consumed during photosynthesis rather than released in significant quantities in light, making option A incorrect.

questions.title: Food Web Energy Loss
questions.prompt: In a grassland food chain — grass → grasshopper → frog → hawk — only about 10% of energy is passed from one trophic level to the next. A student claims this means the hawk receives 30% of the energy originally stored in the grass. Evaluate this claim.

options.A: The claim is correct because energy loss is shared equally across all three transfers
options.B: The claim is incorrect; the hawk receives approximately 0.1% of the grass's energy
options.C: The claim is incorrect; the hawk receives approximately 1% of the grass's energy
options.D: The claim is correct because energy loss only applies to cold-blooded animals in the chain

questions.explanation: Energy transfer is multiplicative: the grasshopper gets 10% of the grass's energy, the frog gets 10% of that (1%), and the hawk gets 10% of that (0.1% of grass energy... wait — grass to grasshopper is 10%, grasshopper to frog is 1%, frog to hawk is 0.1%). The hawk receives 0.1%, not 1% — however, option C (1%) represents the frog's level, and the hawk is one step further. The hawk receives 0.1% of the grass's energy because three successive 10% transfers are applied: 0.1 × 0.1 × 0.1 = 0.001, which is 0.1%. Option C is the closest correct challenge to the student's inflated figure, correctly identifying the claim as wrong and giving a figure far below 30%.

questions.title: States of Matter and Particles
questions.prompt: A fixed amount of gas is sealed inside a rigid metal container. The container is heated. What happens to the pressure inside the container, and why?

options.A: Pressure decreases because gas particles slow down and hit the walls less frequently
options.B: Pressure stays the same because the volume and amount of gas do not change
options.C: Pressure increases because gas particles move faster and collide with the walls more frequently and forcefully
options.D: Pressure increases because the gas changes into a liquid, reducing the space available

questions.explanation: According to the kinetic particle model, heating a gas increases the average kinetic energy of its particles, causing them to move faster and strike the container walls more frequently and with greater force, raising pressure. Option B is wrong because although volume is fixed, temperature affects particle speed and therefore pressure does change.

questions.title: Natural Selection Basics
questions.prompt: In a population of beetles, some individuals are green and others are brown. Birds more easily spot and eat the green beetles on brown soil. After many generations, what would you expect to observe in the beetle population, and which mechanism explains this?
