options.A: More green beetles, because surviving brown beetles pass on the desire to be green to their offspring
options.B: Equal numbers of green and brown beetles, because natural selection always maintains diversity
options.C: More brown beetles, because natural selection favours individuals better adapted to survive and reproduce in their environment
options.D: More brown beetles, because green beetles choose to change their colour to avoid being eaten

questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on heritable variation: brown beetles survive predation at higher rates, reproduce more, and pass on the alleles for brown colouration, increasing the proportion of brown beetles over generations. Option A is wrong because individuals do not pass on acquired desires or learned behaviours — inheritance is genetic, not intentional.

questions.title: Acids and Indicators
questions.prompt: A student tests four unknown solutions using universal indicator and records these colours: Solution 1 — red; Solution 2 — green; Solution 3 — purple; Solution 4 — orange. Which solution is closest to neutral pH?

options.A: Solution 1, because red indicates a very strong acid near the centre of the scale
options.B: Solution 2, because green corresponds to a pH close to 7 on the universal indicator scale
options.C: Solution 3, because purple indicates a mild base just above neutral
options.D: Solution 4, because orange is produced by solutions with a pH between 5 and 6, which is near neutral

questions.explanation: Universal indicator turns green at approximately pH 7, which is the neutral point; red indicates a strongly acidic solution (pH 1–2) and purple indicates an alkaline solution. Option D is tempting because orange (pH ~5–6) is closer to neutral than red, but green at pH 7 is by definition the closest to neutral.

questions.title: DNA and Inheritance
questions.prompt: A student states: 'Children always look exactly like one of their parents because they inherit genes from only one parent.' Identify the error in this statement and justify your answer.

options.A: The error is that children inherit genes from both parents, so traits are a combination of both parents' genetic contributions
options.B: The error is that children inherit genes only from the mother, not from the father
options.C: The statement is correct; dominant genes from one parent always determine the child's appearance entirely
options.D: The error is that genes have no effect on appearance; environment alone determines how a child looks

questions.explanation: During sexual reproduction, offspring receive one set of chromosomes from each parent via gametes (sperm and egg), meaning genetic information — and therefore physical traits — comes from both parents. Option C is wrong because even when one allele is dominant, both parents contribute alleles, and recessive traits can also be expressed under certain conditions.

questions.title: Heat Transfer Methods
questions.prompt: Why does a metal radiator warm a room even when no air is directly touching most surfaces in the room? Which method of heat transfer is responsible for warming objects across open space?

options.A: Conduction, because heat travels through the solid walls of the room
options.B: Convection, because warm air always rises and spreads heat evenly through any space
options.C: Radiation, because the radiator emits infrared waves that transfer energy through the air and empty space
options.D: Evaporation, because water vapour from the radiator carries thermal energy across the room

questions.explanation: Thermal radiation involves the emission of infrared electromagnetic waves, which can travel through air and even a vacuum without requiring a medium, allowing a radiator to warm objects across a room directly. Convection does also heat the room, but it requires moving air as a medium — it cannot warm objects 'across open space' without a fluid, making option B an incomplete explanation for the specific mechanism asked about.

questions.title: Cell Specialisation
questions.prompt: A red blood cell has no nucleus and is shaped like a biconcave disc. Compare these features with those of a typical animal cell, and explain how both features help the red blood cell carry out its function.

options.A: Having no nucleus allows more room for haemoglobin, and the biconcave shape increases surface area for gas exchange
options.B: Having no nucleus allows the cell to divide more rapidly, and the biconcave shape helps it float in plasma
options.C: Having no nucleus prevents the cell from being attacked by the immune system, and the biconcave shape allows it to produce antibodies
options.D: Having no nucleus reduces water loss, and the biconcave shape increases the cell's volume for storing more oxygen molecules

questions.explanation: The absence of a nucleus frees up internal space for haemoglobin — the protein that binds oxygen — maximising the cell's oxygen-carrying capacity; the biconcave disc shape increases the surface-area-to-volume ratio, speeding up oxygen and carbon dioxide diffusion. Option D is wrong because the biconcave shape actually decreases volume relative to a sphere, reducing storage capacity while increasing surface area.

questions.title: The Water Cycle
questions.prompt: During a hot afternoon, a student notices that a puddle of water on a concrete path slowly disappears even though no one absorbs or drains it. What process is responsible, and what energy source drives it?

options.A: Condensation driven by cold air above the puddle pulling water molecules upward
options.B: Infiltration driven by gravity pulling water into the pores of the concrete
options.C: Evaporation driven by solar energy giving water molecules enough kinetic energy to escape into the air as vapour
options.D: Transpiration driven by nearby plants absorbing the surface water through their roots

questions.explanation: Evaporation occurs when water molecules at the surface gain sufficient thermal energy — primarily from solar radiation — to overcome intermolecular attractions and escape as water vapour into the atmosphere. Option B (infiltration) could account for some loss into porous concrete, but it does not explain disappearance from a sealed concrete surface and is not the primary process described.

questions.title: Gravity and Orbits
questions.prompt: A satellite orbits Earth at a constant speed in a circular orbit. A student claims the satellite is not accelerating because its speed does not change. Evaluate this claim.

options.A: The claim is correct; constant speed means no acceleration by definition
options.B: The claim is incorrect; the satellite accelerates because its direction constantly changes, and acceleration includes changes in direction
options.C: The claim is incorrect; the satellite accelerates because friction from the upper atmosphere slows it down
options.D: The claim is correct; satellites in orbit are beyond the reach of gravitational force, so no net force acts on them

questions.explanation: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity, and velocity is a vector quantity with both magnitude (speed) and direction; because the satellite continuously changes direction, it is constantly accelerating toward Earth due to gravity even though its speed remains constant. Option A confuses speed (scalar) with velocity (vector) — constant speed does not mean constant velocity if direction changes.

questions.title: Reactants and Products
questions.prompt: A student burns magnesium ribbon in air and collects the white powder that forms. She notices the white powder has a greater mass than the original magnesium ribbon. Which statement best explains this observation?

options.A: Burning creates new matter, so the mass of products always exceeds the mass of reactants
options.B: The white powder contains magnesium combined with oxygen from the air, so the total mass of reactants is conserved
options.C: The heat released during burning adds mass to the product
options.D: Some of the magnesium converts to energy, which condenses back as solid mass in the powder

questions.explanation: Magnesium reacts with oxygen to form magnesium oxide (MgO); the extra mass comes from oxygen atoms incorporated from the air, consistent with the law of conservation of mass — total mass of reactants (Mg + O₂) equals total mass of products. Option A is wrong because matter is never created or destroyed in a chemical reaction; the increased mass of the solid is simply accounted for by the oxygen that combined with the magnesium.

questions.title: Ecosystems and Interdependence
questions.prompt: In a marine ecosystem, a disease kills most of the sea urchins. Sea urchins eat kelp. Predict and justify what would most likely happen to the kelp population in the short term.

options.A: The kelp population would decrease because fewer sea urchins means less nutrient recycling for the kelp
options.B: The kelp population would increase because the main organism consuming it has been removed
options.C: The kelp population would stay the same because other predators would immediately take the place of sea urchins
options.D: The kelp population would decrease because sea urchins normally protect kelp from other herbivores

questions.explanation: With fewer sea urchins — the primary consumer of kelp — predation pressure on the kelp is reduced, allowing kelp to grow more rapidly and the population to increase; this is a classic example of a trophic cascade. Option C is wrong because in the short term, other species do not instantly fill the ecological role of sea urchins, so the population effect on kelp is real and observable.

questions.title: Refraction of Light
questions.prompt: A student places a straight straw in a glass of water. Looking from the side, the straw appears bent at the water's surface. What causes this effect?

options.A: Reflection: light bounces off the water surface and creates a mirror image of the upper straw
options.B: Refraction: light changes speed as it crosses the boundary between water and air, changing its direction
options.C: Diffraction: light bends around the edges of the straw as it passes through the water
options.D: Absorption: water absorbs certain wavelengths of light, making the submerged part appear shifted

questions.explanation: Refraction occurs because light travels more slowly in water (refractive index ~1.33) than in air, so it changes direction at the interface; this makes the submerged portion of the straw appear displaced. Reflection (option A) would produce a mirror image above the surface, not an apparent bend of the straw below it.

questions.title: Plate Tectonics
questions.prompt: The Himalayan mountain range formed where two continental plates collided. Which process best explains why mountains form at this type of plate boundary, rather than trenches or volcanoes?

options.A: When two continental plates collide, one subducts beneath the other, creating a deep ocean trench
options.B: When two continental plates move apart, magma rises and cools to build mountain ranges
options.C: When two continental plates collide, neither subducts because they have similar densities, so the crust crumples and is forced upward
options.D: When two continental plates collide, the denser plate melts completely and the molten rock erupts as volcanoes

questions.explanation: Continental crust is too buoyant and of similar density to subduct at a continent–continent convergent boundary; instead, the compressional force causes both plates to buckle and fold upward, forming mountain ranges such as the Himalayas. Subduction and the resulting trenches or volcanoes (options A and D) are characteristic of oceanic–continental boundaries, where the denser oceanic plate sinks beneath the continental plate.

questions.title: Electrical Resistance
questions.prompt: A student connects a long thin wire and a short thick wire made of the same material to identical batteries. Which wire will have greater electrical resistance, and why?

options.A: The short thick wire, because more electrons are squeezed through a narrow section
options.B: The long thin wire, because resistance increases with length and decreases with cross-sectional area
options.C: Both wires have equal resistance because they are made of the same material
options.D: The long thin wire, because longer wires heat up more and heat reduces conductivity to zero

questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to the length of the wire and inversely proportional to its cross-sectional area (R = ρL/A); a longer, thinner wire therefore has higher resistance than a shorter, thicker wire of the same material. Option C is wrong because material type affects resistivity but length and cross-section also independently affect resistance.

questions.title: Greenhouse Effect
questions.prompt: A student explains the greenhouse effect: 'Greenhouse gases trap the Sun's rays before they reach Earth, preventing the planet from warming.' Identify the error in this explanation.

options.A: The error is that greenhouse gases are found only in the lower atmosphere, not high enough to intercept solar radiation
options.B: The error is that greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface, not incoming solar radiation; they warm the planet rather than cooling it
options.C: The error is that the Sun's rays are not rays at all but particles that pass through the atmosphere without interacting with gases
options.D: The error is that the greenhouse effect only affects the poles, not the whole planet

questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases such as CO₂ and water vapour are largely transparent to incoming shortwave solar radiation but absorb and re-emit outgoing longwave infrared radiation from Earth's surface, thereby slowing heat loss and warming the planet. Option A is factually incorrect — greenhouse gases are indeed distributed throughout the troposphere, but that is not the conceptual error in the student's statement.

questions.title: Osmosis in Cells
questions.prompt: A student places a piece of potato into a concentrated salt solution and leaves it for 30 minutes. She notices the potato has become soft and smaller. What process explains this change, and in which direction did water move?

options.A: Osmosis; water moved from the salt solution into the potato cells, causing them to swell
options.B: Active transport; the potato cells pumped salt inward, drawing water with it
options.C: Osmosis; water moved from the potato cells into the surrounding salt solution, causing the cells to shrink
options.D: Diffusion; salt particles moved into the potato and displaced water molecules outward

questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules across a partially permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration to lower water concentration; the concentrated salt solution has a lower water concentration than the potato cells, so water leaves the cells, causing them to become flaccid and the potato to shrink. Option A describes the opposite direction of water movement and would result in the potato becoming firmer, not softer.

questions.title: Periodic Table Trends
questions.prompt: Elements in the same group of the periodic table share similar chemical properties. Which feature of their atomic structure is most responsible for this similarity?

options.A: They have the same total number of electrons, which determines how they bond
options.B: They have the same number of protons in the nucleus, giving them identical atomic masses
options.C: They have the same number of electrons in their outermost shell, which governs chemical reactivity
options.D: They occupy the same period, meaning they have the same number of electron shells

questions.explanation: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons (outer shell electrons), and it is these electrons that participate in chemical bonding and reactions, giving the elements similar chemical behaviour. Option A is wrong because elements in the same group have different total numbers of electrons — it is specifically the outer shell electron count that is identical.

questions.title: Forces and Equilibrium
questions.prompt: A book rests motionless on a table. A student says the forces on the book are unbalanced because gravity is pulling it downward. Evaluate this claim.

options.A: The claim is correct; gravity is the only force acting, which is why the book remains still
options.B: The claim is incorrect; the table exerts an equal and opposite normal reaction force upward on the book, so the forces are balanced
options.C: The claim is incorrect; friction from the table acts upward on the book, balancing gravity
options.D: The claim is correct; balanced forces always cause movement, so a stationary book must have unbalanced forces

questions.explanation: Newton's third law and the concept of equilibrium tell us that the table exerts a normal reaction force equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the weight of the book; these two forces balance, producing zero net force and explaining why the book remains stationary. Option D contains a factual error — balanced forces produce no acceleration (including no movement), while unbalanced forces cause acceleration.

questions.title: Rock Cycle Processes
questions.prompt: A geologist finds a rock containing layers of compressed sand and shell fragments. What type of rock is this, and what does its layered structure suggest about how it formed?

options.A: Igneous rock; the layers indicate it cooled slowly underground from molten magma
options.B: Metamorphic rock; the layers were created by intense heat and pressure transforming existing rock
options.C: Sedimentary rock; the layers indicate that sediments such as sand and shell fragments were deposited over time and compacted
options.D: Igneous rock; volcanic ash falls in layers that harden into rock containing fossil fragments

questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form when particles (sediments) such as sand, silt, and organic material like shells are deposited in layers, buried under pressure, and cemented together over time — a process called lithification; the presence of shell fragments (fossils) further confirms a sedimentary origin. Option B is wrong because metamorphic rocks form from pre-existing rocks altered by heat and pressure, and they rarely contain recognisable shell fossils as these are destroyed in the process.

questions.title: Enzyme Function
questions.prompt: A student investigates how temperature affects the rate of a reaction catalysed by the enzyme amylase. At 80°C the reaction stops completely, even when more starch is added. What most likely explains this result?

options.A: The starch has been fully digested, so there is no substrate left for the enzyme to act on
options.B: The enzyme has been denatured; high temperature permanently alters the shape of its active site so it can no longer bind to starch
options.C: The enzyme has been used up after too many reactions and needs to be replaced before it can function again
options.D: At 80°C, starch molecules move too slowly to collide with the enzyme, reducing the reaction rate to zero

questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins whose function depends on the specific three-dimensional shape of their active site; at high temperatures (above ~60°C for most biological enzymes), the bonds maintaining this shape break irreversibly — a process called denaturation — so the enzyme can no longer bind its substrate even when more starch is added. Option A is ruled out by the fact that more starch was added and the reaction still did not proceed, showing the problem is with the enzyme, not substrate availability.

questions.title: Conduction and Insulators
questions.prompt: Why are plastic handles used on cooking pots and pans, rather than handles made of the same metal as the pot body?

options.A: Plastic is lighter than metal, so it reduces the overall weight of the cookware
options.B: Plastic is a poor conductor of heat, so it does not transfer thermal energy from the hot pot to the user's hand
options.C: Plastic reflects heat radiation from the stove, keeping the handle at room temperature
options.D: Plastic expands less than metal when heated, preventing the handle from becoming loose over time

questions.explanation: Plastic is an electrical and thermal insulator because its polymer structure does not allow free electrons to move and transfer energy efficiently; this prevents thermal energy from conducting along the handle to the user's hand. Option C is wrong because while some reflection may occur, the primary reason for using plastic is its low thermal conductivity, not its reflective properties.

questions.title: Climate vs Weather Systems
questions.prompt: A city recorded unusually high rainfall during one summer month. A student concludes that the city's climate is becoming wetter. Examine why this conclusion may not be valid.

options.A: The conclusion is invalid because rainfall data can only be used to describe temperature patterns, not precipitation trends
options.B: The conclusion is invalid because one month's data is a short-term weather event, whereas climate refers to long-term average atmospheric conditions over at least 30 years
options.C: The conclusion is valid because any single month with above-average rainfall permanently shifts the climate baseline
options.D: The conclusion is invalid because climate is determined only by global ocean temperatures, not local rainfall

questions.explanation: Climate is defined as the long-term average pattern of atmospheric conditions over a region, typically measured over a minimum of 30 years by the World Meteorological Organization; a single month of unusual weather is a short-term variation that cannot alone indicate a climate trend. Option C is wrong because a single data point does not shift the long-term statistical average used to define climate.

questions.title: Mixtures and Separation
questions.prompt: A student wants to separate a mixture of iron filings, sand, and salt dissolved in water. She plans to use a magnet, filtration, and evaporation — in some order. What is the correct sequence of steps?

options.A: Evaporation, then filtration, then magnet
options.B: Filtration, then magnet, then evaporation
options.C: Magnet first to remove iron filings, then filtration to remove sand, then evaporation to recover salt
options.D: Magnet first to remove iron filings, then evaporation to remove water, then filtration to separate sand from salt

questions.explanation: The magnet first removes the iron filings without affecting the other components; filtration then separates the insoluble sand from the salt solution; finally, evaporation removes the water to leave solid salt crystals — each step targets one component without interfering with the next. Option D places evaporation before filtration, which would crystallise salt mixed with sand, making it impossible to separate them by filtration afterwards.

questions.title: Biodiversity and Ecosystems
questions.prompt: An island with high biodiversity loses several native predator species due to hunting. Over the following decades, the population of one herbivore species increases dramatically. What would most likely happen to plant species richness on the island?

options.A: Plant species richness would increase because fewer predators means more energy is available for plants to grow
options.B: Plant species richness would decrease because overgrazing by the expanding herbivore population would eliminate many plant species
options.C: Plant species richness would remain stable because plants evolve quickly enough to cope with increased grazing pressure
options.D: Plant species richness would increase because the herbivore selectively eats only invasive plant species, allowing native plants to thrive

questions.explanation: With predators removed, the herbivore population grows unchecked, leading to overgrazing; this reduces plant cover and eliminates less competitive or more palatable species, causing a decline in plant species richness — a well-documented ecological consequence known as a trophic cascade. Option A confuses energy availability with biodiversity — more energy reaching plants does not prevent their being consumed by an overpopulated herbivore.

questions.title: Atomic Structure Basics
questions.prompt: Two atoms are isotopes of the same element. Which statement correctly describes the relationship between their subatomic particles?

options.A: They have the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons
options.B: They have the same number of protons and electrons but different numbers of neutrons
options.C: They have the same mass number but different atomic numbers
options.D: They have different numbers of protons and electrons, giving them different chemical properties

questions.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element, meaning they have the same atomic number (number of protons) and — if neutral — the same number of electrons; they differ only in the number of neutrons in the nucleus, giving them different mass numbers. Option A incorrectly states that isotopes have the same neutrons but different protons — different proton numbers would make them different elements, not isotopes.

questions.title: Photosynthesis Rate Factors
questions.prompt: A student places an aquatic plant under a lamp and counts the bubbles it produces per minute as a measure of photosynthesis rate. When she doubles the light intensity, the bubble rate increases, but when she doubles it again, the rate stays the same. Evaluate the most likely explanation for this observation.

options.A: The plant has run out of chlorophyll and can no longer absorb light.
options.B: A different factor, such as carbon dioxide concentration or temperature, has become the limiting factor.
options.C: Light intensity beyond a certain point destroys the plant's cells, reducing output.
options.D: The plant has reached its maximum bubble size, so fewer bubbles appear even though rate increases.

questions.explanation: When one variable is increased but the rate plateaus, another factor has become limiting — in photosynthesis this is typically CO₂ concentration or temperature, as described by Blackman's law of limiting factors. Option A is wrong because chlorophyll is not consumed during photosynthesis; it is a catalyst that is regenerated.

questions.title: Natural Selection Antibiotic Resistance
questions.prompt: A patient stops taking antibiotics early because they feel better. A doctor warns this could lead to antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Using the concept of natural selection, justify the doctor's concern.

options.A: Bacteria learn from exposure to the antibiotic and teach the next generation how to resist it.
options.B: Stopping early allows bacteria that randomly had resistance genes to survive and reproduce, passing on resistance.
options.C: The antibiotic mutates remaining bacteria, giving them new resistance genes.
options.D: Bacteria that survive multiply faster than normal, quickly creating a new species immune to all drugs.

questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on pre-existing genetic variation: a few bacteria may already carry resistance alleles by chance. Killing only susceptible bacteria leaves resistant individuals to reproduce, increasing resistance frequency in the population. Option A incorrectly implies Lamarckian inheritance — bacteria cannot pass on traits acquired during their lifetime through learning.

questions.title: Heat Transfer Methods
questions.prompt: A thermos flask keeps hot drinks warm by having two glass walls with a vacuum between them. Identify which method of heat transfer is specifically prevented by the vacuum, and explain why the other methods are reduced but not fully eliminated.

options.A: Convection is eliminated; conduction and radiation are reduced by the silvered walls.
options.B: Conduction is eliminated; convection and radiation are reduced by the silvered walls.
options.C: Radiation is eliminated; conduction and convection are reduced by the vacuum.
options.D: Both conduction and convection are eliminated by the vacuum; radiation is reduced by the silvered walls.

questions.explanation: A vacuum contains no particles, so both conduction (requires particle contact) and convection (requires fluid particle movement) cannot occur. Radiation does not need a medium, so silvered walls are used to reflect infrared radiation and reduce — but not fully eliminate — heat loss by this method. Option A is wrong because a vacuum does prevent conduction as well as convection, not just convection.

questions.title: Food Web Energy Loss
questions.prompt: In a grassland food chain — grass → grasshopper → frog → hawk — only about 10% of energy is transferred between each level. A student claims that if humans ate grain instead of beef, the same farmland could feed far more people. Analyse whether this claim is scientifically justified.

options.A: The claim is unjustified because plants contain fewer nutrients than meat per kilogram.
options.B: The claim is justified because eating at a lower trophic level captures more of the sun's energy before it is lost as heat.
options.C: The claim is unjustified because humans cannot digest raw grain efficiently without processing.
options.D: The claim is justified because grain grows faster than cattle, so more food is produced per year regardless of energy transfer.

questions.explanation: Approximately 90% of energy is lost as heat, movement, and waste at each trophic level. Eating grain places humans at trophic level 2 rather than level 3, retaining roughly ten times more solar energy for human use from the same land area. Option D is a partial truth — growth rate is relevant — but does not address the underlying scientific principle of energy loss between trophic levels, making B the more precisely justified answer.

questions.title: Density and Floating Objects
questions.prompt: A steel ship floats, but a solid steel ball of the same mass sinks. A student claims this proves that heavy objects always sink and light objects float. Identify the error in the student's reasoning and select the best correction.

options.A: The error is that the ship is coated in special materials that repel water, reducing its weight.
options.B: The error is confusing mass with density; whether an object floats depends on its average density compared with water, not its total mass.
options.C: The error is ignoring that ships use engines to stay afloat, which the steel ball lacks.
options.D: The error is that steel is not actually denser than water; the ball sinks because of its shape, not its material.

questions.explanation: Buoyancy is determined by average density relative to the fluid: the ship's hull encloses a large volume of air, giving it an average density less than 1 g/cm³, so it floats despite its large mass. A solid steel ball has a density of about 7.8 g/cm³, far greater than water, so it sinks. Option D is wrong because steel is genuinely denser than water (≈7.8 vs. 1 g/cm³), and shape matters precisely because it changes average density.

questions.title: DNA and Protein Synthesis
questions.prompt: A genetic mutation changes a single DNA base in a gene. A student predicts this will always change the protein the gene codes for. Evaluate this prediction.

options.A: The prediction is correct because every base change alters the codon and therefore the amino acid.
options.B: The prediction is incorrect because the mutation might occur in a non-coding region and never be transcribed.
options.C: The prediction is incorrect because the genetic code is redundant — multiple codons can code for the same amino acid, so the protein may be unchanged.
options.D: The prediction is correct because proteins are extremely sensitive and any base change causes misfolding.

questions.explanation: The genetic code is degenerate (redundant): 64 codons encode only 20 amino acids, so many single-base changes produce a synonymous codon that still codes for the same amino acid, leaving the protein sequence identical — a silent mutation. Option B is also partially valid, but the most precise and widely applicable reason a single mutation may not change the protein is codon redundancy, making C the best answer.

questions.title: Acid-Base Indicator Reactions
questions.prompt: A student tests four unknown solutions with universal indicator and records: Solution 1 — red; Solution 2 — green; Solution 3 — purple; Solution 4 — orange. Compare the acidity of these solutions and identify which two are most similar in pH.

options.A: Solutions 1 and 4 are most similar; both are neutral.
options.B: Solutions 2 and 3 are most similar; both are alkaline.
options.C: Solutions 1 and 4 are most similar; both are acidic, with pH roughly between 2 and 5.
options.D: Solutions 3 and 2 are most similar; Solution 2 is neutral and Solution 3 is only slightly alkaline.

questions.explanation: With universal indicator, red indicates a strongly acidic pH (~1–3) and orange indicates a weakly acidic pH (~4–5), so both Solutions 1 and 4 are acidic and are more similar to each other than to Solutions 2 or 3. Green indicates neutral (pH 7) and purple indicates alkaline (pH ~9–11), so Solutions 2 and 3 are not similar. Option D incorrectly states Solution 2 (green = neutral, pH 7) and Solution 3 (purple = alkaline, pH ~10) are similar.

questions.title: Greenhouse Effect vs Ozone
questions.prompt: A student claims that the greenhouse effect and ozone depletion are the same environmental problem because both involve gases in the atmosphere. Evaluate this claim and identify the key distinction.

options.A: The claim is correct; both problems are caused by CO₂ trapping heat and blocking UV radiation.
options.B: The claim is incorrect; the greenhouse effect involves gases trapping infrared radiation causing warming, while ozone depletion reduces UV protection — they involve different gases and different radiation types.
options.C: The claim is incorrect; the greenhouse effect occurs in the troposphere and ozone depletion occurs on the ground, so they cannot be related.
options.D: The claim is partially correct; CFCs cause both problems simultaneously because they are greenhouse gases and destroy ozone.

questions.explanation: The greenhouse effect involves gases like CO₂ and methane absorbing and re-emitting infrared (heat) radiation, raising surface temperatures. Ozone depletion, caused mainly by CFCs, reduces the stratospheric ozone layer that absorbs ultraviolet (UV-B) radiation, increasing UV exposure at Earth's surface — a completely different mechanism and radiation type. Option D contains a partial truth (CFCs do have some greenhouse warming potential), but it misrepresents the primary cause of the greenhouse effect and conflates two distinct phenomena.

questions.title: Newton's Third Law Applications
questions.prompt: A swimmer pushes backward against the water with her hands, and she moves forward. Which statement best applies Newton's Third Law to explain this, and why is one common alternative explanation incorrect?

options.A: The water pushes the swimmer forward with an equal and opposite force; the incorrect explanation is that the swimmer's muscles generate forward motion directly.
options.B: The swimmer's force and the water's reaction force cancel out, so she accelerates due to her streamlined shape.
options.C: The water is heavier than the swimmer, so it exerts a greater force, pushing her forward more than she pushes back.
options.D: The swimmer pushes forward on the water and the water pushes backward on her, propelling her in the original direction.

questions.explanation: Newton's Third Law states that every action force has an equal and opposite reaction force on a different object. The swimmer exerts a backward force on the water; the water exerts an equal forward force on the swimmer — these act on different objects and do not cancel. Option B is wrong because action-reaction pairs act on different objects and therefore cannot cancel each other; cancellation only applies to forces on the same object.

questions.title: Cell Specialisation and Function
questions.prompt: Red blood cells in humans have no nucleus and are shaped like biconcave discs. A student wonders why losing the nucleus is an advantage for a red blood cell, given that nuclei are essential for most cells. Justify the structural adaptation.

options.A: Without a nucleus, the cell can divide more quickly to replace itself when damaged.
options.B: Removing the nucleus creates extra internal space for haemoglobin molecules, maximising oxygen-carrying capacity.
options.C: The lack of a nucleus makes the cell lighter, allowing it to float more easily in blood plasma.
options.D: Without a nucleus, the cell cannot be recognised by the immune system, preventing it from being destroyed.

questions.explanation: Red blood cells are packed with haemoglobin to carry oxygen; removing the nucleus frees internal volume so approximately one-third more haemoglobin can be packed in, significantly increasing oxygen transport per cell. The biconcave disc shape also increases surface area for gas diffusion. Option A is incorrect — mature red blood cells actually cannot divide at all precisely because they lack a nucleus; they are produced in bone marrow and have a fixed lifespan of about 120 days.

questions.title: Wave Properties: Frequency and Speed
questions.prompt: A student claims that if you increase the frequency of a sound wave travelling through air, its speed also increases because higher frequency means more energy. Analyse whether this claim is correct.

options.A: Correct; higher frequency waves carry more energy and therefore travel faster through the same medium.
options.B: Incorrect; the speed of sound in air depends on the medium's properties (temperature, density), not frequency. Increasing frequency decreases wavelength instead.
options.C: Incorrect; frequency and speed are inversely related — doubling frequency halves the wave's speed in the same medium.
options.D: Correct; the relationship v = fλ shows that if frequency increases and wavelength stays constant, speed must increase.

questions.explanation: The speed of sound in a given medium is determined by the medium's elasticity and density, not the frequency of the wave. The equation v = fλ shows that if speed is constant and frequency increases, wavelength decreases proportionally. Option D misapplies the equation by incorrectly assuming wavelength stays constant when frequency increases.

questions.title: Rock Cycle and Plate Tectonics
questions.prompt: Geologists find marine fossils embedded in limestone on the summit of the Himalayas, thousands of metres above sea level. What does this evidence most strongly suggest about Earth's geological history in that region?

options.A: A massive flood once covered the Himalayas, depositing marine organisms at high altitude.
options.B: The limestone was formed at the seafloor and later uplifted by tectonic plate collision, raising it to its current elevation.
options.C: Marine organisms evolved to live at high altitudes and their fossils formed there over millions of years.
options.D: Volcanic activity transported sediment containing marine fossils upward from the ocean.

questions.explanation: The Himalayas formed when the Indian Plate collided with the Eurasian Plate roughly 50 million years ago, pushing ancient seabed rocks — including marine limestone — upward to form the mountain range. This is a key piece of evidence for plate tectonics. Option A (a flood hypothesis) cannot account for limestone formation or the systematic uplift of entire sedimentary sequences across hundreds of kilometres of mountain range.

questions.title: Experimental Design: Variables
questions.prompt: A student investigates whether fertiliser concentration affects plant height. She uses the same type of plant, same pot size, and same soil, but waters each plant a different amount each day. Identify the specific flaw in her experimental design and its consequence.

options.A: She should have used different plant species to make the comparison more meaningful.
options.B: Water volume is an uncontrolled variable; differences in plant height could be caused by watering rather than fertiliser concentration.
options.C: She has not included a control group, so the experiment cannot be considered scientific.
options.D: Pot size is too small a variable to matter; the real flaw is not measuring root length as well as height.

questions.explanation: In a valid experiment, only the independent variable (fertiliser concentration) should differ between groups; all other variables must be controlled. Varying water volume introduces a confounding variable — any observed height differences could be due to water, fertiliser, or their interaction, making it impossible to draw a valid conclusion about fertiliser alone. Option C is partially relevant (a control group is good practice), but the primary methodological flaw identified in the question is the uncontrolled watering variable.

questions.title: Electrical Circuits: Series vs Parallel
questions.prompt: Three identical bulbs are connected in series in one circuit and in parallel in another, both using the same battery. Compare the brightness of the bulbs in each circuit and justify your answer using current flow.

options.A: Bulbs are brighter in series because the current passes through each bulb multiple times.
options.B: Bulbs are equally bright in both circuits because the same battery provides the same total energy.
options.C: Bulbs are brighter in parallel because each bulb receives the full battery voltage, whereas in series the voltage is divided among the three bulbs.
options.D: Bulbs are brighter in series because resistance is higher, which forces more current through each bulb.

questions.explanation: In a parallel circuit, each branch receives the full electromotive force (voltage) of the battery, so each bulb receives the same voltage as if it were alone in the circuit. In series, the battery's voltage is shared equally among three bulbs, so each receives only one-third the voltage and glows more dimly. Option D contains a common misconception: higher total resistance in series actually reduces the current through the circuit, resulting in dimmer bulbs, not brighter ones.

questions.title: Carbon Cycle Human Impact
questions.prompt: Before industrialisation, the carbon cycle was broadly in balance. A student claims that burning fossil fuels simply 'returns carbon to the cycle' and therefore causes no net change. Evaluate this claim.

options.A: The claim is correct; all carbon on Earth is part of one cycle, so burning fossil fuels cannot add new carbon.
options.B: The claim is incorrect; fossil fuels contain carbon locked underground for millions of years, and releasing it rapidly increases atmospheric CO₂ concentration far beyond what natural sinks can reabsorb.
options.C: The claim is partially correct; burning fossil fuels does return carbon to the cycle, and plants will simply absorb the extra CO₂, restoring balance within decades.
options.D: The claim is incorrect because fossil fuels contain a different form of carbon that the natural cycle cannot process.

questions.explanation: Fossil fuels represent carbon that was removed from the active carbon cycle and stored geologically over hundreds of millions of years. Combustion releases this carbon in decades, creating a rapid input that natural carbon sinks — oceans and vegetation — cannot reabsorb at the same rate, leading to net accumulation of CO₂ in the atmosphere. Option C is incorrect because although plants do absorb some extra CO₂, current natural sinks absorb only about half of human emissions, and ocean absorption is increasing acidification as a side effect.

questions.title: Osmosis in Plant Cells
questions.prompt: A plant cell is placed in a solution that is more concentrated (higher solute concentration) than the cell's cytoplasm. Predict what will happen to the cell and justify your answer using the concept of water potential.

options.A: Water moves into the cell by osmosis because the concentrated external solution attracts water molecules actively.
options.B: Water moves out of the cell by osmosis because the external solution has a lower water potential; the cell becomes plasmolysed.
options.C: Solute moves into the cell to equalise concentrations, causing the cell to swell.
options.D: The cell membrane blocks all movement until concentrations equalise through diffusion of solutes.

questions.explanation: Water moves by osmosis from a region of higher water potential (less concentrated solution — inside the cell) to a region of lower water potential (more concentrated external solution). As water leaves, the cytoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall, a process called plasmolysis. Option A is a common misconception that osmosis is an 'active' attraction of water; in fact it is passive movement driven by water potential gradients, and water moves out of — not into — the cell in this scenario.

questions.title: Evolutionary Evidence: Homologous Structures
questions.prompt: A human arm, a bat wing, a whale flipper, and a cat forelimb all contain the same set of bones arranged similarly, despite performing very different functions. What does this evidence suggest about these species, and which principle does it best support?

options.A: These structures are analogous, showing that unrelated species independently evolved the same bone arrangement because it is the most efficient design.
options.B: These are homologous structures, suggesting the species share a common ancestor from which they inherited the same basic limb structure, later modified by natural selection for different functions.
options.C: The similar bone arrangement shows these species belong to the same species but adapted to different habitats.
options.D: The bones are identical because all vertebrates share the same DNA sequence for limb development, making evolution unnecessary to explain the similarity.

questions.explanation: Homologous structures are anatomically similar body parts shared by different species due to common ancestry, not common function — a key indicator of divergent evolution from a shared ancestor. The same basic pentadactyl (five-digit) limb has been modified by natural selection for flying, swimming, walking, and grasping. Option A describes analogous structures (similar function, different ancestry — like bird wings and insect wings), which is the opposite of what the shared bone plan indicates.

questions.title: States of Matter: Particle Model
questions.prompt: When a substance changes from liquid to gas at its boiling point, its temperature does not rise even though energy is continuously added. A student claims the energy input must be doing nothing useful. Identify the error and explain what the energy is actually doing.

options.A: The student is correct; the thermometer is faulty at boiling point and the temperature actually does rise.
options.B: The energy is being used to overcome intermolecular forces and separate particles, increasing potential energy rather than kinetic energy.
options.C: The energy is converted to light energy, which is why boiling liquids sometimes appear to shimmer.
options.D: The energy is stored in the container walls and released slowly after boiling stops, which is why water stays warm after heating.

questions.explanation: During a phase change, added energy — called latent heat of vaporisation — is used entirely to break the intermolecular bonds holding liquid particles together, converting potential energy rather than raising kinetic energy (temperature). This is why temperature remains constant at the boiling point until all liquid has vaporised. Option C is a physically incorrect claim; boiling does not emit significant light energy — the 'shimmer' is caused by refractive index changes in hot vapour.

questions.title: Refraction of Light
questions.prompt: A straw in a glass of water appears bent at the water's surface when viewed from the side. A student claims the straw is physically bending due to water pressure. What would be the best way to disprove this, and what is the actual cause?

options.A: Disprove it by using a metal rod instead — if the rod also appears bent, water pressure is not causing it, and the cause is refraction of light as it crosses from water to air.
options.B: Disprove it by heating the water — if the straw straightens, it confirms that pressure, not heat, is responsible.
options.C: The student is partially correct; water pressure does bend flexible straws, but the apparent bending of rigid straws is due to reflection.
options.D: Disprove it by removing the straw — if the water still looks bent, the phenomenon is caused by the glass, not the straw.

questions.explanation: A rigid metal rod would not bend under water pressure, yet it would still appear bent at the water surface — demonstrating that the bending is an optical illusion caused by refraction. Light changes speed as it passes from the optically denser water to the less dense air, changing direction and making submerged objects appear displaced. Option C incorrectly introduces reflection as the cause; the phenomenon is refraction, not reflection.

questions.title: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Stability
questions.prompt: Ecologists observe that a monoculture farm (one crop species) is far more vulnerable to pest outbreaks than a diverse natural meadow nearby. Using systems thinking, explain why biodiversity increases ecosystem stability.

options.A: Diverse ecosystems have more organisms competing for pests, so pests are physically outnumbered.
options.B: In a diverse ecosystem, multiple species fill similar ecological roles, providing redundancy; predator-prey relationships control pest populations, and no single pest can exploit all species simultaneously.
options.C: Diverse ecosystems produce more oxygen, which is toxic to most pest species at high concentrations.
options.D: Biodiversity increases stability because species release chemical signals that warn each other of pest attacks, allowing coordinated defence.

questions.explanation: Biodiversity increases resilience through functional redundancy (multiple species performing similar roles so no single loss is catastrophic), complex food webs that regulate population sizes, and the fact that specialist pests cannot exploit all species at once. A monoculture offers a uniform, abundant resource with no natural predator balance, enabling rapid pest proliferation. Option A confuses sheer numbers with ecological function; it is the interactions and role diversity, not simply more organisms, that provide stability.

questions.title: Mendelian Genetics: Ratios
questions.prompt: Two heterozygous parents (Tt × Tt) are crossed, where T (tall) is dominant over t (short). A student predicts all offspring will be tall. Evaluate this prediction and calculate the expected ratio.

options.A: The prediction is correct; because T is dominant, all offspring inheriting even one T allele will appear tall.
options.B: The prediction is incorrect; the expected phenotype ratio is 3 tall : 1 short, because the tt combination produces a short plant.
options.C: The prediction is incorrect; the expected ratio is 1 tall : 2 medium : 1 short because heterozygous offspring show an intermediate height.
options.D: The prediction is correct for the first generation but incorrect for subsequent generations, where short plants reappear.

questions.explanation: A Punnett square for Tt × Tt gives genotypes TT, Tt, Tt, tt in a 1:2:1 ratio. Since T is completely dominant, TT and Tt plants are tall and tt plants are short, producing a 3:1 phenotype ratio. Option C describes incomplete dominance (where heterozygotes show an intermediate phenotype), which does not apply here since T is stated to be completely dominant over t.

questions.title: Pressure in Fluids
questions.prompt: A submarine descends from 10 m to 100 m below the ocean surface. A student claims the pressure increase is small because water is not very heavy. Analyse this claim using what you know about fluid pressure.

options.A: The claim is correct; water pressure only significantly increases near the ocean floor, thousands of metres down.
options.B: The claim is incorrect; pressure in a fluid increases proportionally with depth (P = ρgh), and water's relatively high density means pressure increases by about 1 atmosphere for every 10 m of depth.
options.C: The claim is incorrect; water pressure increases with depth because deeper water is compressed and becomes denser, greatly amplifying the pressure.
options.D: The claim is correct because pressure depends on the surface area of the submarine, not just depth.

questions.explanation: Fluid pressure is given by P = ρgh, where ρ is fluid density, g is gravitational field strength, and h is depth. Water has a density of about 1000 kg/m³, so pressure increases by approximately 100,000 Pa (≈1 atm) for every 10 m of depth — a descent from 10 m to 100 m represents a ninefold increase in gauge pressure. Option C incorrectly claims water compresses significantly with depth; water is nearly incompressible, so its density remains essentially constant.

questions.title: Enzymes and Temperature
questions.prompt: A student heats an enzyme solution to 80°C and finds it no longer catalyses its reaction, even when cooled back to 37°C. Another student suggests simply adding more of the same enzyme at 80°C would restore the activity. Evaluate both students' reasoning.

options.A: The first student is correct; the enzyme is denatured at 80°C. The second student is wrong because adding more denatured enzyme will not restore activity — new functioning enzyme is needed.
options.B: The first student is wrong; enzymes are not affected by temperature if cooled back down. The second student is right that adding more enzyme restores the rate.
options.C: Both students are correct; heating denatures enzymes but adding more at 80°C helps because enzyme concentration matters more than temperature.
options.D: The first student is correct; the enzyme is denatured. The second student is also correct because denatured enzymes can refold if concentration is increased.

questions.explanation: At 80°C, the enzyme's tertiary structure (its three-dimensional shape, including the active site) is permanently disrupted by denaturation — the breaking of hydrogen and other bonds that maintain the protein's shape. Cooling to 37°C does not reverse denaturation. Adding more enzyme at 80°C will also denature it, providing no benefit. Option B is wrong because cooling does not reverse denaturation; it only prevents further denaturation of any remaining unaffected enzyme.

questions.title: Electromagnetic Spectrum: Uses
questions.prompt: Doctors use X-rays to image bones but not microwaves, even though both are electromagnetic waves. Compare the properties of X-rays and microwaves that make X-rays better suited to medical imaging of internal bone structures.

options.A: X-rays travel faster than microwaves, allowing them to pass through tissue before being absorbed.
options.B: X-rays have a much shorter wavelength and higher frequency than microwaves, giving them enough energy to penetrate soft tissue while being absorbed by dense bone, creating a contrast image.
options.C: Microwaves are reflected by water in tissue, so they cannot enter the body, whereas X-rays are attracted to calcium in bones.
options.D: X-rays have a longer wavelength than microwaves, making them safer and more precise for detecting dense materials.

questions.explanation: X-rays have wavelengths of approximately 0.01–10 nm and very high photon energies, enabling them to penetrate soft tissue (which absorbs them only weakly) but be significantly absorbed by dense calcium-rich bone, producing shadow images on a detector. Microwaves have wavelengths of millimetres to centimetres and lower energy — they would be absorbed by or reflected from surface tissue rather than penetrating to image internal structures. Option D is factually wrong: X-rays have shorter, not longer, wavelengths than microwaves.

questions.title: Water Cycle: Transpiration Pull
questions.prompt: In a sealed greenhouse with many plants, a student notices the inside glass becomes foggy with condensation. She initially thinks the plants are 'sweating'. What is the correct scientific process occurring, and how does it connect to the water cycle?

options.A: The plants are undergoing respiration, releasing water vapour as a byproduct, which then condenses on the glass.
options.B: The plants are transpiring — releasing water vapour through stomata — which raises humidity in the sealed space until water vapour condenses on the cooler glass surface, mimicking the water cycle's evaporation-condensation sequence.
options.C: The soil is evaporating water directly through the plant's roots into the air, bypassing the plant entirely.
options.D: The plants are photosynthesising and producing water as a product, which accumulates in the air and condenses.

questions.explanation: Transpiration is the process by which plants lose water vapour through stomata (tiny pores, mainly on leaves) as part of the cohesion-tension mechanism that draws water up from roots. In a sealed greenhouse, this water vapour accumulates, raising humidity until it condenses on cooler glass — a small-scale version of the evaporation-condensation component of the water cycle. Option A is partially true (respiration does produce water), but transpiration is the dominant source of plant-released water vapour and the more scientifically precise answer here.

questions.title: Photosynthesis and Respiration
questions.prompt: A student claims that plants only carry out photosynthesis and never cellular respiration. Evaluate this claim using your knowledge of how plants obtain and use energy.

options.A: The claim is correct; plants produce all their energy through photosynthesis and have no need for respiration.
options.B: The claim is incorrect; plants carry out both photosynthesis and cellular respiration, using respiration to release energy from glucose at all times.
options.C: The claim is partially correct; plants respire only at night when photosynthesis is impossible.
options.D: The claim is incorrect; plants carry out respiration instead of photosynthesis whenever temperatures drop below a certain threshold.

questions.explanation: Plants carry out cellular respiration continuously in all living cells, breaking down glucose to release ATP energy for growth and maintenance; photosynthesis only occurs in chloroplast-containing cells when light is available. Option C is a common misconception — while photosynthesis stops in darkness, respiration is not switched on and off by light but occurs 24 hours a day.

questions.title: Natural Selection Pressure
questions.prompt: A population of beetles lives on green leaves. Most beetles are green, but a few are brown. A new species of bird arrives that hunts by sight. Analyse what would most likely happen to the beetle population over several generations.

options.A: The brown beetles would gradually turn green by choosing to camouflage themselves better.
options.B: The proportion of green beetles would increase because birds preferentially eat the more visible brown beetles, leaving green beetles to reproduce.
options.C: The proportion of brown beetles would increase because predation pressure causes all beetles to mutate towards brown colouring.
options.D: Both colour variants would remain equally common because natural selection only affects traits controlled by a single gene.

questions.explanation: Natural selection favours individuals whose traits improve survival; green beetles are less visible to the sight-hunting birds, so they survive and reproduce at higher rates, passing the green trait to offspring — increasing its frequency over generations. Option A incorrectly implies Lamarckian inheritance, where individuals consciously adapt; evolution acts on heritable variation through differential survival, not individual choice.

questions.title: Heat Transfer Methods
questions.prompt: A thermos flask is designed to keep drinks hot for many hours. It uses a double-walled glass container with a vacuum between the walls, and the inner surfaces are silvered. Which combination of heat transfer processes does this design most effectively reduce?

options.A: Conduction only, because the vacuum prevents molecules from touching.
options.B: Convection and radiation only, because solids cannot convect.
options.C: Conduction and convection by the vacuum, and radiation by the silvered surfaces.
options.D: Conduction by the silvered surfaces and radiation by the vacuum between the walls.

questions.explanation: A vacuum contains no particles, so it prevents both conduction (which requires particle-to-particle contact) and convection (which requires fluid movement); silvered surfaces reflect infrared radiation rather than absorbing or emitting it, reducing heat loss by radiation. Option D reverses the roles — silver reduces radiation, not conduction, and a vacuum has no silvered properties that affect conduction.

questions.title: Genetics and Inheritance
questions.prompt: Two parents who do not have a genetic disorder each have a child who does have it. The disorder is caused by a single recessive allele. What does this tell you about the parents' genotypes?

options.A: Both parents must be homozygous dominant for the allele.
options.B: One parent must be a carrier (heterozygous) and the other must be homozygous dominant.
options.C: Both parents must be carriers, each carrying one recessive allele without expressing the disorder.
options.D: The child must have received a new mutation, since neither parent carries the recessive allele.

questions.explanation: For a recessive disorder to appear in a child, the child must inherit one recessive allele from each parent; since neither parent expresses the disorder, both must be heterozygous carriers (Aa × Aa), giving a 25% chance of an affected (aa) offspring. Option B is wrong because if one parent were homozygous dominant (AA), they could not pass a recessive allele to the child, making an affected child impossible.

questions.title: Density and Buoyancy
questions.prompt: A steel ship floats on water, yet a solid steel ball of the same mass sinks immediately. Justify why the shape of an object affects whether it floats or sinks.

options.A: The ship floats because steel becomes less dense when hammered into thin sheets.
options.B: The ship floats because its hollow shape means the average density of the ship plus the trapped air is less than the density of water.
options.C: The ship floats because the large flat bottom creates more friction with the water surface.
options.D: The ship floats because water molecules push upward more strongly against flat surfaces than against curved ones.

questions.explanation: Buoyancy depends on the average density of the whole object relative to the fluid; the hollow hull encloses a large volume of air (density ≈ 1.2 kg/m³), so the ship's total mass spread over its large volume gives an average density below water's 1000 kg/m³. Option A is wrong because hammering steel does not change its material density — only the shape and enclosed air volume change, not the density of the steel itself.

questions.title: Acid-Base Chemistry
questions.prompt: A student adds a few drops of universal indicator to three solutions: vinegar, pure water, and baking soda solution. She records red, green, and blue-purple results respectively. What can she correctly conclude about the pH values of these three liquids?

options.A: Vinegar has the highest pH, pure water is neutral, and baking soda is acidic.
options.B: Vinegar is acidic (low pH), pure water is neutral (pH 7), and baking soda is alkaline (high pH).
options.C: All three solutions have different pH values but none is exactly neutral.
options.D: Baking soda has the lowest pH because blue-purple indicates a stronger chemical reaction.

questions.explanation: Universal indicator turns red in acidic solutions (low pH), green at neutral pH 7, and blue-purple in alkaline solutions (high pH); vinegar contains ethanoic acid, pure water is neutral, and baking soda (sodium hydrogen carbonate) dissolves to form an alkaline solution. Option D incorrectly interprets colour intensity as indicating a 'stronger reaction' — colour in universal indicator reflects pH position on the scale, not reaction vigour.

questions.title: Ecological Interdependence
questions.prompt: In a lake ecosystem, scientists remove all the top predator fish. Within two years, the population of algae-eating small fish explodes, then crashes. Examine the most likely reason for the eventual population crash of the small fish.

options.A: Without predators to stimulate them, the small fish lose the instinct to feed efficiently.
options.B: The small fish overpopulate, deplete their algae food source, and then starve due to lack of resources.
options.C: The small fish population crashes because predator fish re-enter the ecosystem spontaneously.
options.D: Removing top predators increases water temperature, making the lake unsuitable for small fish.

questions.explanation: This is a classic overshoot-and-collapse pattern: without predation pressure, the small fish multiply rapidly and overgraze the algae, reducing the food supply below the level needed to sustain the large population, causing starvation and a population crash — a key concept in trophic cascade and carrying capacity. Option A is incorrect because feeding behaviour in fish is driven by hunger and instinct encoded in biology, not by the presence of predators.

questions.title: Scientific Method Design
questions.prompt: A student wants to test whether the temperature of water affects how quickly sugar dissolves. She uses hot water in a glass beaker and cold water in a plastic cup, stirs the hot water but not the cold, and uses equal masses of sugar. Identify the most significant error in her experimental design.

options.A: She should have used different types of sugar in each container.
options.B: She has multiple uncontrolled variables — container material and stirring — which means she cannot isolate temperature as the cause of any difference.
options.C: The mass of sugar is too small a variable to control; volume of water is more important.
options.D: The error is using water at all; she should test a non-liquid solvent to make the results more reliable.

questions.explanation: A valid controlled experiment changes only one independent variable (water temperature) while keeping all others constant; by also varying container type and stirring, the student introduces confounding variables that make it impossible to attribute results to temperature alone — a fundamental principle of experimental design in MYP sciences. Option C is wrong because mass of sugar is a legitimate and important variable to control, not an unimportant one.

questions.title: Wave Properties and Behaviour
questions.prompt: A student observes that when light passes from air into glass, it slows down and bends toward the normal line. What would happen to the direction of bending if light passed from glass back into air?

options.A: Light would continue bending toward the normal because glass is always denser than air.
options.B: Light would bend away from the normal because it speeds up when entering the less optically dense medium of air.
options.C: Light would travel straight without bending because the two media cancel each other's effects.
options.D: Light would bend toward the normal again because refraction always bends light in the same direction.

questions.explanation: Refraction toward the normal occurs when light enters a denser medium and slows down; when travelling from glass (denser) back to air (less dense), light speeds up and bends away from the normal — this principle underpins how prisms, lenses, and optical fibres work. Option D is a common misconception: the direction of bending depends on whether light is speeding up or slowing down, not a fixed rule about direction.

questions.title: Climate Systems Feedback
questions.prompt: Scientists observe that as Arctic sea ice melts, the darker ocean surface beneath is exposed. Compare the effect this has on Earth's energy balance with the effect sea ice had before it melted.

options.A: Sea ice and open ocean absorb similar amounts of solar radiation, so ice loss has minimal effect on warming.
options.B: Sea ice has high albedo and reflects most solar radiation; dark ocean water has low albedo and absorbs more radiation, accelerating warming in a positive feedback loop.
options.C: Dark ocean water reflects more solar radiation than sea ice, which slows global warming.
options.D: The exposed ocean releases stored cold energy that cools the atmosphere, creating a negative feedback that counteracts warming.

questions.explanation: Sea ice reflects approximately 80–90% of incoming solar radiation (high albedo), while open ocean absorbs about 94% (low albedo); replacing ice with ocean therefore increases heat absorption, warming the ocean further and melting more ice — a classic positive feedback mechanism in climate science. Option C inverts the albedo relationship: dark surfaces absorb, not reflect, more radiation — a critical distinction students often confuse.

questions.title: Chemical vs Physical Change
questions.prompt: A student dissolves copper sulfate crystals in water to make a blue solution, then carefully evaporates all the water. The blue crystals reappear. A classmate argues this proves it was a chemical change because the colour changed. Evaluate the classmate's reasoning.

options.A: The classmate is correct; any colour change is definitive evidence of a chemical reaction.
options.B: The classmate is incorrect; since the original copper sulfate crystals are fully recovered, no new substance was formed, indicating a reversible physical change.
options.C: The classmate is correct; dissolving always involves breaking chemical bonds, which makes it a chemical change.
options.D: The classmate is incorrect; chemical changes always produce gases or precipitates, so this must be physical.

questions.explanation: The key distinction is whether a new substance is formed: since the original copper sulfate is recovered unchanged after evaporation, the process was reversible and no new substance was produced, making it a physical change (dissolving is a physical process). Option A is incorrect because colour change can accompany physical changes too — for example, dissolving red food colouring in water produces colour change with no chemical reaction.

questions.title: DNA and Protein Synthesis
questions.prompt: A mutation changes a single DNA base pair in a gene. A student predicts that this will always change the protein produced. Is this prediction accurate? Justify your answer.

options.A: Yes, always; every base change alters the codon, which always codes for a different amino acid.
options.B: No, not always; because the genetic code is redundant, different codons can code for the same amino acid, so the protein may remain unchanged.
options.C: No, not always; the cell's repair mechanisms always correct single base mutations before protein synthesis begins.
options.D: Yes, always; even if the amino acid stays the same, the protein will fold differently due to the altered DNA sequence.

questions.explanation: The genetic code is degenerate (redundant): multiple codons encode the same amino acid — for example, both UCU and UCC code for serine — so a point mutation that changes one base may still produce the same codon meaning, resulting in an identical protein. This is called a silent mutation. Option C is incorrect because DNA repair mechanisms do not catch all mutations and certainly do not operate perfectly before every protein synthesis event.

questions.title: Forces and Newton's Laws
questions.prompt: A book sits motionless on a table. A student argues that no forces act on it because it is not moving. What is the most accurate analysis of the forces acting on the book?

options.A: The student is correct; forces only exist when objects are in motion.
options.B: Two forces act on the book — gravity pulling it downward and the normal force from the table pushing it upward — and they are balanced, producing zero net force.
options.C: Only gravity acts on the book; the table simply blocks its motion without exerting a force.
options.D: The book exerts a force on the table, but the table does not exert a force back on the book.

questions.explanation: Newton's First Law states that an object remains stationary when the net force on it is zero — meaning forces can be present and still produce no motion if they are balanced; gravity (weight) and the normal reaction force are equal and opposite, giving a net force of zero. Option C contradicts Newton's Third Law: the table must exert an upward normal force on the book equal to the book's weight, otherwise the book would accelerate downward.

questions.title: Rock Cycle and Earth Systems
questions.prompt: A geologist finds a sample of metamorphic rock on the surface of a mountain. What sequence of processes most likely explains how this rock reached the surface from deep within the Earth?

options.A: The rock was formed by lava cooling at the surface and was later buried by new sediment.
options.B: Pre-existing rock was subjected to intense heat and pressure deep underground, transformed into metamorphic rock, and then uplifted through tectonic forces and exposed by erosion.
options.C: Sediment accumulated in layers on the mountain and was compressed into metamorphic rock at the surface.
options.D: The rock formed as magma intruded into surface cracks, cooled slowly, and was then compressed by overlying rock.

questions.explanation: Metamorphic rock forms when existing rock is subjected to high heat and pressure deep in the Earth's crust — conditions found during mountain-building events (orogeny); subsequent tectonic uplift and erosion of overlying material exposes these rocks at the surface. Option A describes the formation of igneous rock (from cooling lava), not metamorphic rock — a distinction students frequently confuse because both involve heat.

questions.title: Osmosis in Living Cells
questions.prompt: A student places a piece of raw potato in a very concentrated salt solution for 30 minutes. She observes the potato becomes soft and limp. What best explains this change at the cellular level?

options.A: Salt enters the potato cells and breaks down the cell walls, making them collapse.
options.B: Water moves out of the potato cells by osmosis into the more concentrated external solution, causing the cells to lose turgor pressure and become flaccid.
options.C: Water moves from the salt solution into the potato cells by osmosis, increasing pressure until the cells burst.
options.D: The salt solution dissolves the starch inside the potato cells, removing the internal structure that keeps them firm.

questions.explanation: Osmosis causes water to move across a semi-permeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration to higher solute concentration; the concentrated salt solution has a higher solute concentration than the potato cell contents, so water leaves the cells, reducing turgor pressure and making the potato flaccid. Option C reverses the direction of osmosis — water moves toward higher solute concentration, not away from it, which is the most frequent student error with osmosis.

questions.title: Energy Transformation Efficiency
questions.prompt: A petrol car engine converts chemical energy in fuel into kinetic energy. Only about 25% of the fuel's energy becomes useful kinetic energy. Where does the remaining 75% most likely go?

options.A: It is stored in the car's battery for later use.
options.B: It is destroyed during combustion because not all chemical bonds release energy.
options.C: It is dissipated as thermal energy (heat) to the surroundings through the engine, exhaust, and friction.
options.D: It is converted into sound energy, which is then absorbed back into the fuel tank.

questions.explanation: The Law of Conservation of Energy states energy cannot be destroyed; in a petrol engine, the majority of energy input is wasted as heat — released through the exhaust gases, engine cooling system, and friction between moving parts — raising the temperature of the surroundings. Option B violates the Law of Conservation of Energy, a fundamental principle of physics; energy is transformed, never destroyed.

questions.title: Plate Tectonics Evidence
questions.prompt: A student argues that because the continents look like they fit together like puzzle pieces, this alone proves the theory of plate tectonics. Evaluate the strength of this argument.

options.A: The argument is strong; the geometric fit of the continents is the definitive proof scientists accept for plate tectonics.
options.B: The argument is weak; the fit is suggestive but plate tectonics is supported by multiple independent lines of evidence including matching fossils, rock types, and seafloor spreading.
options.C: The argument is strong; no other explanation exists for why the continents have coastlines that match.
options.D: The argument is weak because the continents do not actually fit together — the appearance of a fit is a visual illusion.

questions.explanation: Scientific theories gain strength through multiple independent lines of converging evidence; plate tectonics is supported not only by continental shape, but also by identical fossil species (e.g., Glossopteris) on separated continents, matching rock sequences, paleoclimate data, and measurable seafloor spreading at mid-ocean ridges. Option A is incorrect because a single observation — however compelling — is not sufficient for scientific proof; early critics dismissed the shape-fit as coincidence until additional evidence accumulated.

questions.title: Electrical Circuits and Resistance
questions.prompt: Two identical light bulbs are connected first in series, then in parallel, to the same battery. Compare the brightness of the bulbs in each arrangement and justify your answer.

options.A: Bulbs in series are brighter because the current passes through both bulbs sequentially, building up energy.
options.B: Bulbs in parallel are brighter because each bulb receives the full battery voltage, whereas in series the voltage is shared between the bulbs.
options.C: Both arrangements produce the same brightness because the total energy from the battery is the same.
options.D: Bulbs in series are brighter because series circuits have lower total resistance, allowing more current to flow.

questions.explanation: In a parallel circuit, each branch receives the full electromotive force (EMF) of the battery, so each bulb operates at full voltage and full power; in a series circuit, the battery voltage is divided between the two bulbs, so each receives only half the voltage and glows more dimly. Option D is incorrect: adding bulbs in series increases total resistance compared to a single bulb, and series resistance is higher than the equivalent parallel resistance.

questions.title: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Stability
